STUDYQURAN:3:44/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r1.claim: Ghayb is what is invisible or hidden, or absent because it lies in the past, future, or another state of being.
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r1.anchor: invisible or hidden, but also what is absent by being in the past, in the future, or

STUDYQURAN:3:44/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r2.claim: The Quran also says the Prophet did not witness the events at Sinai.
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r2.anchor: the Quran also points out that the prophet was not witness to the events at Sinai in 28:44, 46

STUDYQURAN:3:44/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r3.speaker: IK, M
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r3.claim: The most widely accepted account says the Temple priests wanted custody of Mary and cast lots to determine who would care for her.
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r3.anchor: The most widely accepted account is that the priests of the Temple desired to be the custodians of Mary after she entered the Temple (see v. 37) and cast lots to decide who would have the privilege (IK, M)

STUDYQURAN:3:44/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r4.claim: The Bible describes lots used regularly for decisions of varying importance, including selecting people, sacrifices, and divination, not only for intractable choices.
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r4.anchor: In many places the Bible mentions that lots were cast on a regular basis for matters of varying levels of importance (choosing persons—who would be king, who would offer incense in the Temple, who would sacrifice an animal—and also for divination)

STUDYQURAN:3:44/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r5.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r5.claim: Some commentators say Zachariah was not disputed as Mary's caretaker because he was married to her maternal relative; the dispute may instead concern her continuing care or Temple service.
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r5.anchor: Some commentators believe, however, that Zachariah was not disputed as the custodian or caretaker of Mary (Ṭ), since he was the husband of her maternal relative

STUDYQURAN:3:44/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r6.claim: The more widely accepted view is that lots were cast and God's will placed Mary with Zachariah.
STUDYQURAN:3:44/r6.anchor: But it is more widely accepted that indeed they cast lots and it was God’s Will that she be given into the care of Zachariah

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r1.claim: “That” refers to the reports about Imran’s wife, Maryam, Zakariya, Yahya, and the events narrated from the account beginning with God’s choosing Adam and Noah.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r1.anchor: {إن الله اصطفى آدم ونوحا} [آل عمران: 33] ثم جمع

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r2.claim: The phrase means hidden reports about earlier people, unknown to Muhammad and his community and known only to a few learned people among the two scriptural communities.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r2.anchor: فقال: هذه الأنباء من أنباء الغيب: أي من أخبار الغيب، ويعني بالغيب، أنها من خفي أخبار القوم

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r3.claim: God says He revealed these hidden accounts to Muhammad as evidence of his prophethood and truthfulness, removing the excuse of People of the Book who knew how obscure the reports were.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r3.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى ذكره نبيه محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه أوحى ذلك إليه حجة على نبوته، وتحقيقا لصدقه

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r4.claim: Their obscurity supports the proof: Muhammad was unlettered, did not read books, and did not learn these accounts from companions among the People of the Book.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r4.anchor: إذ كان معلوما عندهم أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم أمي لا يكتب فيقرأ الكتب فيصل إلى علم ذلك من قبل الكتب

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī derives ghayb as the verbal noun of ghāba, to be absent from or hidden from something.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r5.anchor: وأما الغيب: فمصدر من قول القائل: غاب فلان عن كذا، فهو يغيب عنه غيبا وغيبة

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r6.claim: Here nuḥīhi means “We send it down to you.”

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r7.claim: The basic sense of waḥy is conveying something from the one who communicates it to its recipient; this can occur through writing, gesture, indication, inspiration, or a messenger.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r7.anchor: وأصل الإيحاء: إلقاء الموحي إلى الموحى إليه، وذلك قد يكون بكتاب وإشارة وإيماء وبإلهام وبرسالة

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r8.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r8.claim: In 16:68, God’s waḥy to the bees means that He inspired them.

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r9.claim: In 5:111, God’s waḥy to the disciples means that He inspired or communicated the knowledge to them.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r9.anchor: بمعنى: ألقيت إليهم علم ذلك إلهاما

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r10.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r10.claim: The rajaz phrase about God’s waḥy to people to praise morning and evening illustrates conveying a command, potentially by indication.

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r11.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r11.claim: In 6:121, the devils’ waḥy to their allies means whispering or casting a suggestion to them.

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r12.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r12.claim: In 6:19, the Qur’an was conveyed to Muhammad by Gabriel from God.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r12.anchor: ألقي إلي بمجيء جبريل عليه السلام به إلي من عند الله عز وجل

TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r13.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r13.claim: The noun waḥy names what passes from sender to recipient; Arabs also call script and writing waḥy because the written words are fixed in what is inscribed.
TAB-FULL:v5p400#2/r13.anchor: وأما الوحي: فهو الواقع من الموحي إلى الموحى إليه، ولذلك سمت العرب الخط والكتاب وحيا

TAB-FULL:v5p402/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p402/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p402/r1.claim: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr’s line says poems remain like waḥy on hard stone, illustrating waḥy as writing fixed in its medium.
TAB-FULL:v5p402/r1.anchor: أتى العجم والآفاق منه قصائد بقين بقاء الوحي في الحجر الأصم

TAB-FULL:v5p402/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p402/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p402/r2.claim: Arabic can call a book waḥy, without the alif, when a scribe has written and embellished it; Ruʾba’s line about a finely written Gospel illustrates this usage.
TAB-FULL:v5p402/r2.anchor: كأنه بعد رياح تدهمه … ومرثعنات الدجون تثمه إنجيل أحبار وحى منمنمه

TAB-FULL:v5p403/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r1.claim: Idh yalqūn means “when they were casting”; their aqlām were the lots or arrows used by the Israelites to decide who would care for Maryam, as explained at 3:37.
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r1.anchor: وأما أقلامهم فسهامهم التي استهم بها المتسهمون من بني إسرائيل على كفالة مريم

TAB-FULL:v5p403/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r2.claim: Qatada says the statement that Muhammad was not present refers to Muhammad himself.
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وما كنت لديهم}

TAB-FULL:v5p403/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r3.claim: Mujahid says Zakariya and his companions drew lots with their pens for Maryam when she was brought to them.
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد: {يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] «زكريا وأصحابه استهموا

TAB-FULL:v5p403/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r4.claim: Qatada recounts that Maryam, daughter of their leader, became the subject of a custody dispute; the Israelites drew lots, Zakariya won, and as her sister’s husband he took her in.
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون}

TAB-FULL:v5p403/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r5.claim: Qatada also summarizes the contest as drawing lots over Maryam, with Zakariya winning the right to care for her.
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] قال: «تساهموا على مريم أيهم يكفلها، فقرعهم زكريا»

TAB-FULL:v5p403/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says worshippers in the sanctuary, who wrote revelation, cast their pens to choose who would care for Maryam; God told Muhammad he had not witnessed their dispute.
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم}

TAB-FULL:v5p403/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r7.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak says they cast lots with their pens to determine who would care for Maryam, and Zakariya beat the others.
TAB-FULL:v5p403/r7.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم}

TAB-FULL:v5p405/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r1.claim: Muhammad was not present to witness these events; he learned them through God's revelation and instruction.
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r1.anchor: ففي قوله عز وجل: {إذ يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] دلالة على محذوف من الكلام، وهو: «لينظروا أيهم يكفل

TAB-FULL:v5p405/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says they cast lots over Mary, an unseen event of which Muhammad knew only when God informed him.
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] قال: «حيث اقترعوا على مريم،

TAB-FULL:v5p405/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r3.claim: They cast lots to determine who had the strongest claim and was most entitled to care for Mary; the verse leaves that purpose implicit.
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r3.anchor: ففي قوله عز وجل: {إذ يلقون أقلامهم} [آل عمران: 44] دلالة على محذوف من الكلام، وهو: «لينظروا أيهم يكفل

TAB-FULL:v5p405/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r4.claim: Although the implied sense might suggest an accusative, أي is the subject of an interrogative inquiry after verbs of looking, discerning, and knowing.
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r4.anchor: فقد ظن خطأ؛ وذلك أن النظر والتبين والعلم مع «أي» يقتضي استفهاما واستخبارا، وحظ «أي» في الاستخبار الابتداء

TAB-FULL:v5p405/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r5.claim: كفل means to take in or care for; al-Tabari says he established this meaning earlier.
TAB-FULL:v5p405/r5.anchor: وقد دللنا فيما مضى قبل أن معنى يكفل يضم، بما أغنى عن إعادته

TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.claim: Muhammad was absent when Mary's people disputed which of them was most entitled to care for her.
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r1.anchor: يعني بذلك جل ثناؤه: وما كنت يا محمد عند قوم مريم، إذ يختصمون فيها أيهم أحق بها وأولى

TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.claim: This address rebukes disbelieving Jews and Christians: Muhammad reports events he did not witness, without reading their books or learning from their scholars.
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r2.anchor: فتوبيخ منه عز وجل للمكذبين به من أهل الكتابين، يقول: كيف يشك أهل الكفر بك منهم،

TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits from Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr that the revelation disclosed concealed knowledge about their dispute, confirming Muhammad's prophethood and establishing proof against them.
TAB-FULL:v5p405#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير: {وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون} [آل عمران: 44] «أي ما كنت معهم إذ يختصمون فيها

TABATABAI:2:21-25#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:21-25#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:21-25#6/r4.claim: The Qur'an challenges people through accounts of earlier prophets and peoples, declaring such reports unseen to Muhammad and his people before revelation.
TABATABAI:2:21-25#6/r4.anchor: تلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيها إليك ما كنت تعلمها أنت ولا قومك من قبل هذا

TABATABAI:3:44/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:44/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:44/r1.claim: The account of Mary's guardianship is unseen news revealed to Muhammad, like Joseph's story; reports among the People of the Book are unreliable because of alteration, and their books omit Qur'anic details about Zakariya.
TABATABAI:3:44/r1.anchor: عده من أنباء الغيب نظير ما عدت قصة يوسف عليه السلام من أنباء الغيب التي توحى إلى رسول الله

TABATABAI:3:44/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:44/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:44/r2.claim: The Prophet and his people were unlettered and did not know these stories from books; this supports revelation as the source, and the first explanation best fits the verse's context.
TABATABAI:3:44/r2.anchor: على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وقومه كانوا أميين غير عالمين بهذه القصص ولا أنهم قرأوها في الكتب

TABATABAI:3:44/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:44/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:44/r3.claim: A qalam here is a lot-drawing arrow, also called a share or lot; casting their arrows means they drew lots to decide who would care for Mary.
TABATABAI:3:44/r3.anchor: القلم بفتحتين القدح الذي يضرب به القرعة ويسمى سهما أيضا وجمعه أقلام

TABATABAI:3:44/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:44/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:44/r4.claim: The dispute was competition to care for Mary; the men resolved it by lot, and Zakariya won, as the following account says he became her guardian.
TABATABAI:3:44/r4.anchor: إنما هو اختصامهم وتشاحنهم في كفالة مريم وأنهم لم يتناهوا حتى تراضوا بالاقتراع بينهم

TABATABAI:3:44/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:44/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:3:44/r5.claim: Some commentators place the dispute and drawing of lots after Mary grew up, when Zakariya could no longer care for her, because the Qur'an mentions the lot after her birth and guardianship.
TABATABAI:3:44/r5.anchor: وربما احتمل بعضهم أن هذا الاختصام والاقتراع بعد كبرها وعجز زكريا عن كفالتها

TABATABAI:3:44/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:44/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:44/r6.claim: Al-Tabataba'i sees no problem in the Qur'an repeating story details to establish its point, as it does after Joseph's story; the lot can therefore concern the initial guardianship.
TABATABAI:3:44/r6.anchor: وفيه أنه لا ضير في إعادة بعض خصوصيات القصة أو ما هو بمنزلة الإعادة لتثبيت الدعوى

TABATABAI:3:42-60#19/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#19/r8.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:42-60#19/r8.claim: Al-Bāqir explains that the people cast lots with their pens when Mary was orphaned from her father.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#19/r8.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي في قوله تعالى { إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم } عن الباقر عليه السلام يقرعون بها حين أيتمت من أبيها

TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r1.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r1.claim: Al-Bāqir reports that after Mary’s birth, the family disputed who would care for her; they drew lots and Zechariah’s lot won.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r1.anchor: قال لما ولدت اختصموا آل عمران فيها وكلهم قالوا نحن نكفلها فخرجوا وضربوا بالسهام بينهم فخرج سهم زكريا

TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says his preceding explanation supports this account and the preceding report about Mary’s selection.
TABATABAI:3:42-60#20/r2.anchor: أقول وقد مر من البيان ما يؤيد هذا الخبر وما قبلها

TABRISI:3:44/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r1.claim: Anbāʾ is the plural of nabaʾ, meaning reports or news.

TABRISI:3:44/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r2.claim: Waḥy is conveying a meaning secretly; it can mean God sending an angel to a prophet or inspiration, as in the revelation to the bee.
TABRISI:3:44/r2.anchor: والإيحاء هو إلقاء المعنى إلى الغير على وجه يخفى

TABRISI:3:44/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r3.claim: Waḥy can also mean a gesture or signal, as when the people were signaled to glorify God morning and evening.

TABRISI:3:44/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r4.speaker: العجاج
TABRISI:3:44/r4.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj uses waḥy for settling or conveying a quiet direction, in a line about something settling and being held firm.
TABRISI:3:44/r4.anchor:
قال العجاج:
أوحى لها القرار فاستقرت

TABRISI:3:44/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r5.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses waḥy for a gesture sent through fingers.

TABRISI:3:44/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r6.speaker: رؤبة
TABRISI:3:44/r6.claim: Ruʾba uses waḥy for writing, including writing in the scrolls of the Lord.
TABRISI:3:44/r6.anchor:
قال رؤبة:
لقدر كان وحاه الواحي

TABRISI:3:44/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r7.claim: Qalam can mean a writing pen, a lottery arrow, or each person’s own allotted arrow; its root sense is cutting off an end.
TABRISI:3:44/r7.anchor: والقلم الذي يكتب به والقلم الذي يجال بين القوم كل إنسان

TABRISI:3:44/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r8.claim: Qalam also means trimming nails, while the joints of a spear are maqālim; both relate to cutting.
TABRISI:3:44/r8.anchor: والقلم قص الظفر ومقالم الرمح كعوبه وأصله قطع طرف الشيء

TABRISI:3:44/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r9.speaker: أبو علي
TABRISI:3:44/r9.claim: Abū ʿAlī connects the first idh to “you were not”; the second may connect to “they were disputing,” or be a substitute for the first if both events coincided.
TABRISI:3:44/r9.anchor: قال أبو علي إذ في قوله إذ يلقون متعلق بكنت

TABRISI:3:44/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r10.claim: Dhālika refers to the preceding account of Mary, Zechariah, and John.
TABRISI:3:44/r10.anchor: { ذلك } اشارة إلى ما تقدم ذكره

TABRISI:3:44/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r11.claim: God conveys the unseen account to Muḥammad as a proof, reminder, illumination, admonition, and lesson.
TABRISI:3:44/r11.anchor: أي نلقيه عليك معجزة وتذكيرا وتبصرة وموعظة وعبرة

TABRISI:3:44/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r12.claim: The account demonstrates prophethood: Muḥammad had not witnessed these events or learned them from books, and his Meccan audience were not scriptural scholars.
TABRISI:3:44/r12.anchor: بين أهل مكة ولم يكونوا أهل كتاب

TABRISI:3:44/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r13.claim: The pens they cast may be the writing implements with which they wrote the Torah.
TABRISI:3:44/r13.anchor: أقلامهم } التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة في الماء

TABRISI:3:44/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r14.claim: Alternatively, the objects were lottery arrows marked so they could determine who would care for Mary.
TABRISI:3:44/r14.anchor: وقيل أقلامهم أقداحهم للاقتراع جعلوا عليها علامات يعرفون بها من يكفل مريم

TABRISI:3:44/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r15.claim: The clause omits an understood purpose: they cast lots to see whose lot would appear and who would care for Mary.
TABRISI:3:44/r15.anchor: وفيه حذف أي لينظروا أيهم تظهر قرعته ليكفل مريم

TABRISI:3:44/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r16.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:3:44/r16.claim: Qatāda reads the verse as expressing God’s amazement at how eagerly they sought to care for Mary.
TABRISI:3:44/r16.anchor: وهذا تعجيب من الله نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم من شدة حرصهم

TABRISI:3:44/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r17.claim: Another view takes it as amazement that they contested responsibility during a severe crisis, until the best guardian, Zechariah, was chosen for her.
TABRISI:3:44/r17.anchor: وقيل هو تعجيب من تدافعهم لكفالتها لشدة الأزمة

TABRISI:3:44/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r18.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44/r18.claim: Their dispute shows they had reached the point of openly contending over Mary’s care.
TABRISI:3:44/r18.anchor: فيه دلالة على أنهم قد بلغوا في التشاح عليها إلى حد الخصومة

TABRISI:3:44/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44/r19.speaker: الأكثر
TABRISI:3:44/r19.claim: Most say the dispute occurred at Mary’s birth, when her mother brought her to the sanctuary and they contested who would raise her.
TABRISI:3:44/r19.anchor: أحدهما: حين ولادتها وحمل أمها إلى الكنيسة

TABRISI:3:44#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:3:44#2/r1.claim: The verse establishes that casting lots can distinguish competing rights; the author cites sayings from al-Ṣādiq and al-Bāqir in support.
TABRISI:3:44#2/r1.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن للقرعة مدخلا في تميز الحقوق

TABRISI:3:44#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
TABRISI:3:44#2/r2.claim: Some date the dispute to Mary’s adulthood, when Zechariah could no longer raise her.
TABRISI:3:44#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم كان ذلك وقت كبرها وعجز زكريا عن تربيتها

TABRISI:3:44#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44#2/r3.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:3:44#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṣādiq says that when people delegate their matter to God and draw lots, the rightful person’s lot emerges; he calls such a decision just.
TABRISI:3:44#2/r3.anchor: قال الصادق ع: ما تقارع قوم

TABRISI:3:44#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44#2/r4.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:3:44#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṣādiq invokes the Qurʾānic case of Jonah, who drew lots and was among the defeated, as evidence for the practice.
TABRISI:3:44#2/r4.anchor: وقال: أي قضية أعدل من القرعة

TABRISI:3:44#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:3:44#2/r5.speaker: الباقر
TABRISI:3:44#2/r5.claim: Al-Bāqir says Mary was the first subject of a lot, followed by Jonah; he then recounts ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib’s lots over sacrificing his son ʿAbd Allāh, finally resolved by one hundred camels and three repeated draws.
TABRISI:3:44#2/r5.anchor: وقال الباقر: أول من سوهم عليه مريم ابنة عمران

THALABI:v3p67/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p67/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p67/r1.claim: ‘That’ refers to the accounts of Zakariyya, Yahya, Mary, and Jesus; the pronoun in نوحيه refers back to that account, and الغيب means reports of the unseen.
THALABI:v3p67/r1.anchor: ذلك: الذي ذكرت من حديث زكريا ومن حديث ويحيى ومريم وعيسى

THALABI:v3p67/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p67/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p67/r2.claim: The Prophet was not present when they cast lots to decide who would care for Mary; the lots were arrows or drawing-sticks, with قلم as the singular.
THALABI:v3p67/r2.anchor: وما كنت: يا محمد، لديهم: عندهم، إذ يلقون أقلامهم سهامهم وقداحهم للاقتراع في الماء

THALABI:v3p67/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p67/r3.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v3p67/r3.claim: Another explanation says the objects cast into the water were their pens for writing the Torah.
THALABI:v3p67/r3.anchor: وقيل: [أقلامهم التي كانوا يكتبون بها] التوراة

THALABI:v3p67/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v3p67/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v3p67/r4.claim: Their dispute was over who would take responsibility for Mary.
THALABI:v3p67/r4.anchor: وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون: في كفالتها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p250/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p250/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p250/r1.claim: That refers to the account just told about Zakariyya, Mary, and Yahya.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p250/r1.anchor: أشار إلى ما قص من حديث زكريا، ومريم، ويحيى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p250/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p250/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p250/r2.claim: Wahy means conveying a message to someone by messenger, inspiration, writing, or gesture; Qur'anic examples include revelation to Muhammad, inspiration to bees and Moses' mother, a gesture by Zakariyya, and satanic whispering.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p250/r2.anchor: الإيحاء) في اللغة: إلقاء معنى الكلام إلى من تريد إعلامه؛ إما بإرسال رسول، أو بإلهام، أو بكتابة، أو بإشارة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r1.claim: Aqlām is the plural of qalam, from cutting: a writing pen is sharpened at its tip, and a lot arrow is cut at both ends.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r1.anchor: و (القلم) (¬2) أصله من: (القلم)، وهو: قطع للطرف (¬3)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, through Ata, says prophets disputed over Mary's custody; after invoking God and casting their arrows into a spring, Zakariyya's arrow floated while the rest sank, and he won the lot.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء (¬1): هؤلاء كانوا جماعة من الأنبياء، اختلفوا واختصموا في مريم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says they were marked lottery arrows used to identify who would care for Mary.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p251/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬8): هي قداح جعلوا عليها علامات، يعرفون بها من يكفل مريم على جهة القرعة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p253/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p253/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p253/r1.claim: The phrase is elliptical: they cast lots to determine which of them would be assigned Mary's care.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v5p253/r1.anchor: مختصر (¬1)؛ أي: لينظروا أيهم تجب له كفالة مريم (¬2).

QASHANI:3:42-46/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:42-46/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:42-46/r3.claim: The hidden news is the unseen condition of the Prophet's own being, revealed to the Prophet of the spirit.

QASHANI:3:42-46/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:42-46/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:42-46/r4.claim: The spiritual and psychic powers were not in the Prophet's rank when competing for their interests and drawing lots to govern the soul, each trying to command it for its own perceived benefit.
QASHANI:3:42-46/r4.anchor: يتسابقون في سهامهم ويتبادرون في حظوظهم أيهم يدبر مريم النفس ويكفلها بحسب رأيه

QASHANI:3:42-46/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:3:42-46/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:3:42-46/r5.claim: Their dispute takes place in the chest, the locus of conflict between spiritual and psychic powers competing for leadership before and during discipline; with God's aid, spiritual powers prevail after discipline.
QASHANI:3:42-46/r5.anchor: يتنازعون ويتجاذبون في طلب الرياسة عند ظهوره قبل الرياضة وفي حالها، إذ غلبت ملائكة القوى الروحانية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r1.claim: That refers to the preceding account of Zachariah and Mary; these are unseen reports revealed to the Prophet.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r1.anchor: { ذلك } أي: ما قصصنا عليك من حديث زكريا ومريم { من أنباء الغيب } أي: من أخباره { نوحيه إليك } أي: نلقيه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r2.claim: The Prophet was not present to know the events firsthand.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r3.claim: Hannah brought Mary to the Jerusalem sanctuary attendants as a vowed offering; the priests competed for her guardianship and cast lots, which Zachariah won.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r3.anchor: وذلك أن حنة لما ولدت مريم أتت بها سدنة بيت المقدس، وقالت لهم: دونكم هذه النذيرة، فتنافس فيها الأحبار حتى اقترعوا عليها، فخرجت القرعة لزكريا

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r4.claim: The pens were arrows they cast lots with to determine who would care for Mary.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:3:44/r4.anchor: { إذ يلقون أقلامهم } أي: قداحهم التي كانوا يقترعون بها لينظروا أيهم تجب له كفالة مريم.

ELMALILI:3:44/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:44/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:44/r1.claim: Because Muhammad was not present when the people cast lots over Maryam’s care or disputed, Elmalılı treats this account of the unseen as proof that Muhammad is the true, divinely revealed Messenger whom people must obey.
ELMALILI:3:44/r1.anchor: senin vâcibu’l-itâ‘a bir Resûl-i Kibriyâ Muhammed Mustafâ olduğunda ve bu haberlerin vahy-i hak bulunduğunda şüphe yok.

ELMALILI:3:44/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:3:44/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:3:44/r2.claim: After this reminder about the unseen and the dispute over Maryam’s selection, the narrative is to continue by recounting the full truth of Jesus’ story.
ELMALILI:3:44/r2.anchor: Bu ihtar akabinde ve ihtisâm noktasında ıstıfâ-yı Meryem’e müte‘allik olarak Îsâ kıssasının dahi bütün hakikatini anlatmak için şunları yâd et:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r1.speaker: Birçok müfessir
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r1.claim: Many exegetes say Muhammad could not have learned these accounts by reading or hearsay; since he did not witness them, the verse identifies revelation as the source of his knowledge.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r1.anchor: Birçok müfessir bu âyeti şöyle yorumlamışlardır: Hz. Muhammed’in muhatapları onun

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r2.speaker: Muhammed Abduh
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r2.claim: Abduh finds the common reading inconsistent with verses saying polytheists alleged that Muhammad learned elsewhere; he takes the verse to show the information was absent among the People of the Book, rebutting that suspicion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r2.anchor: Muhammed Abduh’a göre, Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de müşriklerin Hz. Muhammed’in bu bilgileri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r3.speaker: M. Reşîd Rızâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r3.claim: Rida says Abduh’s reading too conflicts with some verses: accusations cannot change historical realities, and the Qur’an cites such allegations to expose their absurdity; circumstances around Muhammad refute the claim he borrowed these accounts.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r3.anchor: M. Reşîd Rızâ ise bu yorumun da bazı âyetlerle uyumlu olmadığını belirtir; müşriklerin Hz. Muhammed hakkındaki iftiralarının onun hayatına ilişkin tarihî gerçekleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r4.claim: The Qur’anic account has Zechariah and a nearby group cast lots amid a contest over Mary’s care; by divine decree the duty ultimately falls to Zechariah.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r4.anchor: Kur’an-ı Kerîm’de verilen bilgi, Hz. Zekeriyyâ ile yakın konumdaki bir grup insanın kalemlerini (kura araçları) atarak yani kura çekerek bu görevi üstlenme yarışı içine girdikleri

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r5.claim: Commentators suggest either that Mary’s deceased father Imran was a senior, respected religious leader or that participants recognized her future mission from scriptural prophecies as reasons to seek her care.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r5.anchor: Bu göreve tâlip olma sebebi, Meryem’in vefat etmiş olan babası İmrân’ın kıdemli ve saygı duyulan bir din adamı olması ya da dinî kitaplarda Hz. Meryem ve Hz. Îsâ’nın geleceğini bildiren ifadelerden

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r6.claim: The participants are described as Temple servants or clergy; because they considered themselves Zechariah’s peers and accepted a lot to settle the matter, they were probably senior clerics.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r6.anchor: Kuraya katılanlar Beytülmakdis’in hizmetçileri veya burada görevli din adamlarıdır. Kendilerini Hz. Zekeriyyâ ile aynı düzeyde görüp ancak kura yoluyla çözüme razı olduklarına göre

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r7.claim: One reported lot procedure threw pens used for scripture, or staffs, into water; the owner of the item moving against the current won.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r7.anchor: dinî metinleri yazdıkları kalemlerini veya bastonlarını suya atmaları ve suyun akış yönünün tersine giden kalem veya baston sahibinin kazanmış sayılması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r8.claim: Another reported procedure cast inscribed arrows into water and counted the owner of the first arrow to surface as the winner.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r8.anchor: yahut isimler yazılı okların suya atılması ve kimin oku su yüzüne önce çıkarsa onun kazanmış kabul edilmesidir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r9.claim: Jurists who permit drawing lots when no other criterion can settle a right or duty cite this verse, along with Jonah’s and the ship’s lots.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:3:44/r9.anchor: Bir hak veya vecîbenin belirlenmesinde başka ölçüt bulunamayan durumlarda kura yoluna başvurmanın İslâm’da da câiz olduğu sonucuna ulaşan hukukçular bu âyeti de delil gösterirler

ITQAN:v2p482/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p482/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p482/r3.claim: Ladā and ladun may alternate with ʿinda; the source illustrates them with bodily, spatial, and narrative uses.
ITQAN:v2p482/r3.anchor: وتعاقبها لدى ولدن نحو ﴿ لدى الحناجر ﴾ ﴿ لدى الباب ﴾ ﴿ وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم

ITQAN:v2p482/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p482/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p482/r5.claim: Unlike ʿinda and ladā, ladun only marks an endpoint or starting point.
ITQAN:v2p482/r5.anchor: فعند ولدى تصلح في محل ابتداء غاية وغيرها ولا تصلح لدن إلا في ابتداء غاية

ITQAN:v2p482/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p482/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p482/r6.claim: ʿInda and ladā may function as optional modifiers, whereas ladun cannot.
ITQAN:v2p482/r6.anchor: وعند ولدى يكونان فضلة نحو ﴿ وعندنا كتاب حفيظ ﴾ ﴿ ولدينا كتاب ينطق بالحق ﴾ ولدن لا تكون فضلة

ITQAN:v2p482/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p482/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p482/r7.claim: Ladun is more often governed by min than accusative and has no Qur’anic accusative use; ʿinda is often genitive, while ladā cannot be genitive.
ITQAN:v2p482/r7.anchor: وجر لدن بمن أكثر من نصبها حتى أنها لم تجيء في القرآن منصوبة وجر عند كثير وجر لدى ممتنع

ITQAN:v2p482/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p482/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p482/r8.claim: ʿInda and ladā are declinable, while ladun is indeclinable in the speech of most Arabs; ladun can also appear without an annexed noun or be annexed to a clause.
ITQAN:v2p482/r8.anchor: وعند ولدى يعربان ولدن مبنية في لغة الأكثرين

ITQAN:v2p482/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p482/r9.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v2p482/r9.claim: Al-Raghib says ladun is narrower and more emphatic than ʿinda because it indicates the beginning of an endpoint or action.
ITQAN:v2p482/r9.anchor: وقال الراغب لدن أخص من عند وأبلغ لأنه يدل على ابتداء نهاية الفعل

AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r4.claim: The interrogative ayyuhum follows because a search for knowledge can be followed by a question, as in the cited purpose clauses linalama and liyabluwakum.
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r4.anchor: قال الله تعالى {إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم} لأن كل ما كان

AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r5.claim: In thumma lananziʿanna ... ayyuhum, ayyuhum is fixed on ḍamm, not inflected, because lananziʿanna is not a request for knowledge.
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r5.anchor: فلم يرتفع على مثل ما ارتفع عليه الأول

AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r6.claim: He attaches ashadda to ayy as its complement; some put it in the accusative, which he says is analogical.
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r6.anchor: وجعل {أشد} من صلتها وقد نصبها قوم وهو قياس

AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r7.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r7.claim: Some read nominative aḥsanu as a relative-clause complement of alladhī; the accusative aḥsana makes it governed by the verb.
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r7.anchor: وقد قرىء {تماما على الذي أحسن} فرفعوا وجعلوه من صلة "الذي"

AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r8.speaker: بعض العرب
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r8.claim: Some Arabs say mā anā bi-lladhī qāʾilun laka shayʾan; in the dual they use bi-lladhayni qāʾilāni.
AKHFASH:v1p217#2/r8.anchor: وزعموا ان بعض العرب قال: "ما أنا بالذي قائل لك شيئا"

DAMGHANI:v1p389/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r6.claim: Aqlām can mean arrows used for drawing lots: the people cast them into water to decide who would care for Mary.
DAMGHANI:v1p389/r6.anchor: الأقلام السهام قوله تعالى في سورة آل عمران

DAMGHANI:v1p418/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r10.claim: Alqā can mean to draw lots, as when the people cast their pens to decide who would care for Mary.
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r10.anchor: إذ يقلون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم

DAMGHANI:v1p418/r13.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r13.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r13.claim: The ten listed senses of alqā include whispering, creating, placing, sending down, drawing lots, clothing, entering, throwing, speaking, and seating; this excerpt explains the first seven.
DAMGHANI:v1p418/r13.anchor: ل ق ى على عشرة أوجه وسوس خلق وضع أنزل أقرع كسا أدخل رمى كلم أجلس

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p481#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p481#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p481#2/r2.claim: Qalam can mean a lot or arrow used to draw lots, as in drawing lots over Mary.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p481#2/r2.anchor: ومن الثاني : قوله تعالى : ^ ( إذ يلقون أقلامهم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p105#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p105#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p105#2/r1.claim: They cast lots with their arrows to decide who would take Mary into his care and raise her.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p105#2/r1.anchor: {يلقون أقلامهم} أي: قداحهم، يقترعون على مريم. أيهم يكفلها ويحضنها.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p105#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p105#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p105#2/r2.claim: Aqlām is the plural of qalam; these lots are also called azlām, singular zalam or zulam.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p105#2/r2.anchor: والأقلام واحدها قلم. وهي: الأزلام أيضا؛ واحدها زلم وزلم (2) .

MAJAZ:v1p92/r6.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p92/r6.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p92/r6.claim: Anbāʾ al-ghayb means reports of what is hidden from you.
MAJAZ:v1p92/r6.anchor: «من أنباء الغيب» (44) : من أخبار الغيب، ما غاب عنك

MAJAZ:v1p92/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p92/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p92/r7.claim: Ladayhim means in their presence or with them.

MAJAZ:v1p92/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p92/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p92/r8.claim: Aqlāmuhum means their arrows, used for casting lots.

MAJAZ:v1p92/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p92/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p92/r9.claim: Yakful means to take into one’s care or include.

NAHHAS:v1p374/r21.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p374/r21.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p374/r21.claim: Dhālika may be a predicate of an omitted subject (“that is the matter”), or a subject whose predicate is min anbāʾ al-ghayb.
NAHHAS:v1p374/r21.anchor: في موضع رفع أي الأمر ذلك فهو خبر الأمر

NAHHAS:v1p374/r22.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p374/r22.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p374/r22.claim: Idh is accusative as an adverb meaning “at that time.”
NAHHAS:v1p374/r22.anchor: إذ في موضع نصب أي وما كنت لديهم ذلك الوقت

NAHHAS:v1p374/r23.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p374/r23.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p374/r23.claim: Aqlām is the plural of qalam, related to qalamahu, “he cut it.” The better interpretation is their writing pens, used for revelation, cast into a river to see which followed the current and whose owner would care for Mary.
NAHHAS:v1p374/r23.anchor: جمع قلم من قلمه إذا قطعه وقد ذكرنا أنه قيل أقلامهم سهامهم

NAHHAS:v1p374/r24.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p374/r24.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p374/r24.claim: He prefers writing pens over arrows or lots because the latter are the forbidden azlām, though the people might have cast them without the pagan practice’s intent.
NAHHAS:v1p374/r24.anchor: فأما أن تكون الأقلام القداح فبعيد لأن هذه هي الأزلام التي نهى الله عز وجل عنها

NAHHAS:v1p374/r25.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p374/r25.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p374/r25.claim: Ayyuhum is a subject attached to an omitted verb meaning “they look to see which one”; Sībawayh gives a parallel, and accusative would change the meaning.
NAHHAS:v1p374/r25.anchor: ابتداء وهو متعلق بفعل محذوف أي ينظرون أيهم يكفل مريم وحكى سيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r1.claim: One parse makes dhālika the predicate of an omitted subject, al-amru dhālika; min anbāʾ al-ghayb may be a circumstantial phrase modifying the demonstrative.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن يكون " ذلك " خبر مبتدأ محذوف تقديره: الأمر ذلك. و " من أنباء الغيب " على هذا يجوز أن يكون من تتمة هذا الكلام حالا من اسم الإشارة

SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r2.claim: On that parse, one may pause after dhālika and attach min anbāʾ al-ghayb to what follows; nuḥīhi then explains the previous clause or is circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r2.anchor: ويكون " من أنباء الغيب " متعلقا بما بعده وتكون الجملة من " نوحيه " إذ ذاك: إما مبينة

SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r3.claim: A second parse makes dhālika the subject and min anbāʾ al-ghayb its predicate, with nuḥīhi independent.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r3.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون " ذلك " مبتدأ، و " من أنباء الغيب " خبره

SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r4.claim: On the second parse, the pronoun in nuḥīhi refers to al-ghayb, encompassing stories already mentioned and those yet to come; this is better than returning it to dhālika, which limits it to prior events.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r4.anchor: والضمير في " نوحيه " عائد على الغيب، أي: الأمر والشأن أنا نوحي إليك الغيب

SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r5.claim: The verse presents revelation of earlier peoples’ stories despite the Prophet’s lack of study with learned people or historians.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r5.anchor: ونظهرك على قصص من تقدمك مع عدم مدارستك لأهل العلم والأخبار

SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r6.claim: A third parse makes nuḥīhi the predicate; min anbāʾ al-ghayb may modify it, be circumstantial from dhālika, or describe the object as part of the unseen reports.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r6.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون " نوحيه " هو الخبر، و " من أنباء الغيب " على وجهيه المتقدم

SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r7.claim: The verse implies that the Prophet did not learn the earlier events from people of knowledge and therefore learned them through revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44/r7.anchor: مع عدم مدارستك لأهل العلم والأخبار

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r1.claim: The apparent parse makes idh yalqūna governed by the existential operator governing the preceding adverbial predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما: وهو الظاهر أنه منصوب بالاستقرار العامل في الظرف الواقع خبرا

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r2.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r2.claim: Al-Fārisī instead makes idh governed by kunta; al-Samīn objects that an eventless kāna cannot govern a temporal ظرف, though he thinks al-Fārisī may assume kāna complete, “was present then.”
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r2.anchor: والثاني وإليه ذهب الفارسي أنه منصوب بكنت، وهو عجيب منه لأنه يزعم أنها مسلوبة الدلالة على الحدث فكيف تعمل في الظرف

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r3.claim: The pronoun in ladayhim refers to those disputing about Mary, although they have not been named, because context identifies them.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r3.anchor: والضمير في " لديهم " عائد على المتنازعين في مريم وإن لم يجر لهم ذكر، لأن السياق

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r4.claim: The denials that the Prophet witnessed these events, echoed at 28:46 and 12:102, taunt deniers of revelation: without study or eyewitness access, his knowledge can only come through revelation.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r4.anchor: وما كنت بجانب الطور [القصص: 46] وما كنت لديهم إذ أجمعوا أمرهم [يوسف: 102] وإن كان معلوما انتفاؤه بالضرورة جار مجرى التهكم بمنكري الوحي

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r5.claim: Aqlām is the plural of qalam, a faʿl form with passive sense “something cut”; qalam means cutting, as in clipping and smoothing a nail.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r5.anchor: والأقلام جمع " قلم " وهو فعل بمعنى مفعول أي: مقلوم، والقلم القطع

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r6.claim: Zuhayr’s description of a lion whose claws were not clipped gives poetic evidence for the cutting sense of qalam.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r6.anchor: لدى أسد شاكي السلاح مقذف له لبد أضفاره لم تقلم

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r7.claim: Another proposed etymology relates qalam to qillāma, a weak plant, because the object becomes thin and weak.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r7.anchor: وقيل: سمي القلم قلما تشبيها له بالقلامة وهي نبت ضعيف؛ وذلك أنه يرقق فيضعف

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r8.claim: Commentators differ whether the aqlām were writing pens or lottery arrows like azlām.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#2/r8.anchor: وفي المراد بالأقلام هنا خلاف: هل هي التي يكتب بها أو قداح يستهم بها كالأزلام

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r1.claim: Ayyuhum yakfulu Maryam is governed by an omitted verb and is itself circumstantial; the missing verb may mean “looking to see” or “knowing.”
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة منصوبة المحل؛ لأنها متعلقة بفعل محذوف، ذلك الفعل في محل نصب على الحال تقديره: يلقون أقلامهم ينظرون: أيهم يكفل مريم أو يعلمون

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī supplies yaqūlūna, making the clause quoted speech, as indicated by yalqūna.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r2.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري أن يقدر " يقولون " ، فيكون محكيا به، ودل على ذلك قوله: { يلقون }.

SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r3.claim: The statement that the Prophet was not among them when they disputed is parsed like the parallel statement about their casting lots.
SAMIN-DURR:3:44#3/r3.anchor: وقوله: { وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون } كقوله: { وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون }.

ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r1.claim: The stories of Zachariah, John, Mary, and Jesus are unseen reports; the Prophet's accurate knowledge without reading, despite consensus that he was unlettered, confirms revelation and prophethood.
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r1.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على تثبيت نبوة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لأنه أنبأ بما لا يعلم إلا من كتاب أو وحي وقد أجمعوا أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان أميا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r2.claim: The pens are marked lots used to draw who would care for Mary; qalam relates to shaving or cutting bit by bit.
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r2.anchor: وهي قداح جعلوا عليها علامات يعرلون بها أيهم يكفل مريم على جهة القرعة - وإنما قيل للسهم القلم

ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r3.claim: Qalam relates to repeated trimming of a writing pen and fingernails: whatever is cut away bit by bit has been qalama-ed.
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r3.anchor: وإنما قيل للسهم القلم لأنه يقلم أي يبرى، وكل ما قطعت منه شيئا بعد شيء فقد قلمته،

ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r4.claim: The lots determine who is entitled to care for Mary; kafāla is guaranteeing and undertaking her affairs.
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r4.anchor: أي لينظروا أئهم تجب له كفالة مريم، وهو الضمان للقيام بأمرها، ومعنى

ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r5.claim: Ladayhim means among them or in their presence.

ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r6.claim: The first idh is governed by mā kunt; he attaches the second idh to yakhtaṣimūn, locating the dispute at the angels' speech.
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r6.anchor: إذ نصب بقوله (ما كنت لديهم) و (إذ) الثانية معلقة ب (يختصمون) أي إذ يختصمون إذ قالت الملائكة،

ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r7.claim: Alternatively, the second idh may be governed by mā kunt لديهم, describing an event the Prophet did not witness.
ZAJJAJ:v1p410/r7.anchor: وجائز أن يكون نصب إذ على (وما كنت لديهم). (إذ قالت الملائكة). هذا أيضا مما لم يشاهده.

ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n30/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n30/r1.speaker: Muhammad 'Abduh
ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n30/r1.claim: Abduh reads the aside to the Prophet as stressing that Mary's Qur'anic story comes directly through revelation and is inherently true despite differences from Christian scripture.

ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n31/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n31/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n31/r1.claim: The wording literally means 'they cast their reeds'; Asad sees it as an ancient Semitic lot-drawing custom, perhaps like pre-Islamic Arab divination with blunt arrows.
ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n31/r1.anchor: The phrase rendered above as "they drew lots" reads literally, "they cast their reeds" - obviously a reference to an ancient Semitic custom

ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n31/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n31/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n31/r2.claim: The pronoun 'they' refers to the priests, one of whom was Zachariah.
ASAD-NOTES:3:44#n31/r2.anchor: The pronoun "they" relates to the priests, of whom Zachariah was one

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r1.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r1.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r1.claim: Scientific thinking is empirical rationality: experimental sciences systematically produce, revise, and generalize knowledge to describe, explain, predict, and control the shared lived world.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r1.anchor: العلوم الإخبارية التي تضطلع بهذا العالم الأولي الفيزيقي عديدة، فيزيوكيماوية وحيوية وإنسانية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r2.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r2.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r2.claim: Mathematical thinking is chiefly characterized as logical, while scientific thinking specifically takes shape in the empirical sciences.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r2.anchor: التفكير الرياضي يُنعت أساسًا بأنه تفكير منطقي، أما التفكير العلمي بألف ولام التعريف، فهو أسلوب التفكير المتعين والمتجسد في العلوم التجريبية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r3.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r3.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r3.claim: Scientific inquiry proposes bold hypotheses but submits them to sensory and experimental evidence, correcting or replacing them when facts expose error.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r3.anchor: أسلوب التفكير العلمي التجريبي ينصت لشهادة الحواس ومعطيات الوقائع، فتعين موضع الخطأ والكذب في الفرض حين يتعارض معها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r4.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r4.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r4.claim: Science is not a completed structure of certain facts; it is a succession of increasingly successful hypotheses that correct, absorb, or surpass earlier limits and move closer to truth.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r4.anchor: فليس العلم بناءً مشيدًا من حقائق قاطعة، بل هو نسق من فروض ناجحة، كل يوم فروض أنجح من سابقتها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r5.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r5.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r5.claim: Scientific progress has no final endpoint: each answer raises further questions, so research continues and continually transforms its present.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r5.anchor: كل إجابة يتوصل إليها العلم تطرح تساؤلات أبعد، فيؤدي كل تقدم إلى تقدم أعلى. ومهما علونا في مدارج التقدم لن تغلق المعامل أبوابها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r6.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r6.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r6.claim: Experimental facts act as a severe, decisive judge of error, while scientific thought joins reason and understanding with experiment, senses, and reality.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r6.anchor: في خضم هذه الحركية التقدمية تقوم وقائع التجريب بدور ناقد قاس لا يعرف الرحمة حين تعيينه لمواضع الخطأ

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r7.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r7.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r7.claim: Scientific thinking also models civic values: planning, method, creativity, plural debate, and letting shared reality judge competing proposals; every achievement remains provisional and revisable.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r7.anchor: قيم من قبيل التخطيط والتفكير الممنهج والإبداع والتنافس لحل المشاكل في تعددية الرأي والرأي الآخر، ثم الالتجاء لمحك الواقع المشترك

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r8.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r8.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r8.claim: Scientific method is highly effective for practical and scholarly engagement with reality, but its subject is the physical, empirically shared world rather than every level of human existence.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r8.anchor: ينصب على العالم الواقعي أو الكون الفيزيقاني

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r9.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r9.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r9.claim: Human existence spans possible, emotional, ethical, aesthetic, metaphysical, ideological, and unseen worlds as well as the physical; mature civilization needs the sciences, religion, philosophy, values, art, and ideology together.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r9.anchor: وبخلاف العالم الواقعي الفيزيقي ثمة العالم الممكن والمرجو، عالم ما ينبغي أن يكون، عالم العاطفة والوجدان، عالم القيم والمُثل، عالم الفن الاستطيقي، العالم الميتافيزيقي، العالم الأيديولوجي، وأخيرًا عالم الغيب

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r10.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r10.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r10.claim: Science and religion serve different but necessary civilizational needs; conflict between them signals a crisis, and neither should be sacrificed to the other.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r10.anchor: نتفق جميعًا على الاحتياج الحضاري للعلم والدين معًا، وليس مجديًا البتة التضحية بأيها على مذبح الآخر

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r11.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r11.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r11.claim: Scientific thought is empirical, falsifiable, probabilistic, and relative, whereas religious thought rests on assent, affirmation, absoluteness, and certainty; civilization needs both horizons.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r11.anchor: فقد تبدت أيضًا سماته التي تتبلور في الاختبارية والقابلية للتكذيب والنسباوية والاحتمالية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r12.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r12.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r12.claim: Religious enlightenment takes human reason seriously, remains open to changing circumstances, and listens to other views; it opposes dogmatic exclusivity, rigid certainties, and closed literalism.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r12.anchor: النظر بعين الاعتبار للعقل الإنساني ولقدراته وإمكانياته المتوالية دومًا، وبالتالي الانفتاح على متغيرات الواقع، والقدرة على الاستماع للرأي الآخر

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r13.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r13.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r13.claim: An enlightened religious approach uses methods that renew the sacred text for changing times and places, keeping religion a genuinely universal message.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r13.anchor: يتعامل مع النص الديني بمناهج قادرة على التحديث وبعث الحياة فيه، ليتجدد مع كل جديد ويغدو ملائمًا لكل العصور

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r14.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r14.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r14.claim: Modern hermeneutics treats reading as a living encounter in which text and reader, past and present, meet; this encounter is an ontological situation and part of the text’s history.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r14.anchor: ينصهر فيها النص والقارئ معًا، الماضي والحاضر في علاقة متجددة هي موقف أنطولوجي (أي وجودي) للقارئ المفسر

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r15.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r15.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r15.claim: Hermeneutic dialogue keeps texts open to new interpretations: they do not simply state truth but establish renewed relations with it, speaking in each reader’s present while remaining connected to living reality.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r15.anchor: ثمة حوار مستمر مع النص يجعله مفتوحًا دائمًا لفهم جديد وتأويل جديد، وبالتالي تغدو النصوص معاصرة دومًا، لكل من يقرؤها مُجددًا فهي لا تقول الحقيقة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r16.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r16.speaker: فردريش شلايرماخر
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r16.claim: Schleiermacher, as relayed by Tillich, held that religion is no inexplicable mystery and that religious language is ordinary language, changing with the forces it expresses.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r16.anchor: أكد شلايرماخر أن الدين ليس سرًّا ملغزًا، وليس ثمة لغة قدسية وضعت بين دفتي كتاب

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r17.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r17.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r17.claim: Gadamer’s 1960 Truth and Method helped establish hermeneutics as a wide-ranging field with schools and strong influence on cultural discussion and literary criticism.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r17.anchor: حتى ظهر عام ١٩٦٠ كتاب «هانز جيورج جادامر» الخطير، وهو «الحقيقة والمنهج» لتستوي الهيرومنيوطيقا علمًا له مدارسه واتجاهًا واسعًا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r18.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r18.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r18.claim: Because hermeneutics arose in theology and Protestantism, the author presents it as a methodical example of religious enlightenment and a way to root modern science in Arab civilization through renewed readings of foundational texts.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r18.anchor: إن الهيرومنيوطيقا التي نشأت أصلًا في أعطاف اللاهوت، وترعرعت في أفياء البروتستانتية تكاد تكون تمثيلًا منهجيًّا للاستنارة الدينية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r19.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r19.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r19.claim: Religious enlightenment should acknowledge that science has its own methods, grounds for growth, and clear boundaries, allowing scientific and religious activity to coexist without religious oversight.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r19.anchor: الموقف الديني المستنير موقف حضاري راشد، يدرك خاصية الاستقلال والتميز التي يتسم بها العلم والبحث العلمي والتفكير العلمي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r20.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r20.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r20.claim: Experimental testability and falsifiability demarcate the natural sciences; religion, metaphysics, philosophy, art, ideology, and ethics can be more important but serve other purposes and need not meet that criterion.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r20.anchor: فكل ما لا يقبل الاختبار التجريبي والتكذيب لا يعد علمًا؛ أي لا يحمل مضمونًا معرفيًّا وقدرة تفسيرية عن العالم التجريبي، وهي حدود لن يتخطاها ما لا يحمل هذه الوظيفة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r21.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r21.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r21.claim: History shows both church opposition to early modern science and nineteenth-century scientific materialism that overreached against religion, while seventeenth-century England saw natural science and Protestant reform flourish together.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r21.anchor: فبينهما نجد القرن السابع عشر، حيث أحرز نجاح العلم الطبيعي خطًى جوهرية بلغت الذروة في إنجلترا التي اكتمل فيها نسق الفيزياء الكلاسيكية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r22.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r22.speaker: فرانكلين باومر
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r22.claim: Baumer notes that Bacon and leading members of the Royal Society saw natural science as studying God’s creation, yet Bacon still protected science from theological interference.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r22.anchor: «فرانكلين باومر»، اعتقد «فرنسيس بيكون» مع جهابذة الجمعية الملكية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r23.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r23.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r23.claim: The collapse of the closed mechanical universe under discoveries in atomic and radiation physics, relativity, and quantum mechanics revealed science’s ongoing, revisable, probabilistic character.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r23.anchor: لقد انجلت طبيعة التفكير العلمي الحقة إثر انهيار الآلة الميكانيكية الكلاسيكية المغلقة كتصور للكون

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r24.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r24.speaker: جاستون باشلار
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r24.claim: Bachelard argues that science advances by repeatedly correcting prior knowledge rather than emerging from an unstructured state of ignorance; its self-criticism drives continual progress.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r24.anchor: لذلك ينتهي «جاستون باشلار» (١٨٨٤–١٩٦٢) — شيخ فلاسفة العلم في فرنسا — إلى أن العلم يتنكر دائمًا لما ينجزه، من حيث دأبه على اختباره ونقده وتصويبه

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r25.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r25.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r25.claim: The author contrasts God’s enduring, fixed created existence with human science as contingent, changing, growing activity: existence is being, while science is becoming.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r25.anchor: الوجود المتعين صنيعة الله، والعلم المتنامي صنيعة الإنسان. الوجود قديم والعلم حادث، الوجود ثابت والعلم متغير، الوجود باق والعلم نام

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r26.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r26.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r26.claim: Both attacking science for contradicting scripture and stopping at scientific theories that seem to match scripture are sterile; enlightened religion instead recognizes science’s independence and distinct path.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r26.anchor: بدلًا من النزاع الضاري والعقيم الذي خاضته الكنيسة لتناقض بعض نظريات العلم الحديثة مع ظاهر النصوص الدينية، نجد كثيرين اليوم يستنفدون جهدًا أشد عقمًا للتوقف عند تشابه بعض النظريات

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r27.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r27.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r27.claim: Scientific thought also needs enlightenment: it should respect the sacred religious domain, recognize its own limits, and avoid rashly denying what lies beyond them.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r27.anchor: وأخيرًا لنا أن نطالب التفكير العلمي بمثل هذه الاستنارة، وأن يعترف هو الآخر باستقلالية وحرمة المجال الديني، ويدرك حدود وقصورات التفكير العلمي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r28.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r28.speaker: بول فييرآبند
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r28.claim: Feyerabend rejects the idea that science is all-encompassing or superior to every other form of knowledge; it is one cultural tradition among several, including religion, custom, and popular wisdom.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r28.anchor: ليؤكد أن العلم ليس كل شيء وليس معرفة فائقة تقهر كل ما عداها، بل هو تقليد ضمن تقاليد حضارية أخرية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r29.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r29.speaker: بول فييرآبند
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r29.claim: Feyerabend says a free society requires plural cultural traditions and cooperation among them and among nations, rather than rule by scientific rationality alone or Western dominance.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r29.anchor: المجتمع الحر حقًّا لا يقوم على نظرية جزئية هي النظرة العلمية فقط، أو على عقلانية واحدة هي العقلانية العلمية، بل يقوم المجتمع الحر على تعددية التقاليد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r30.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r30.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r30.claim: Since people need both science and religion, each must recognize the other’s independence and treat it with respect; this is scientific and religious enlightenment alike.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c4/r30.anchor: لأن الإنسان في حاجة إلى العلم وإلى الدين، فهو في حاجة لاعتراف كليهما بالآخر، والاستقلالية والاحترام المتبادل بينهما

QIRAAT-ER:3:44:20#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:3:44:20#1/r1.speaker: vhr
QIRAAT-ER:3:44:20#1/r1.claim: The pronoun hāʾ has kasra in ladayhim or ḍamma in ladayhum; both are canonical dialectal forms in the seven-reader system.
QIRAAT-ER:3:44:20#1/r1.anchor: Vowel shift on the hāʾ: ladayhim (kasra) vs. ladayhum (ḍamma) — dialectal variation in the 3mp pronoun suffix

IBNHISHAM:v1p580#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p580#2/r1.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p580#2/r1.claim: Zakariya first cared for Mary, but during a severe crisis among the Israelites he could not support her; they drew lots, and Jureij the monk, an Israelite carpenter, was selected.
IBNHISHAM:v1p580#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: كفلها هاهنا جريج الراهب، رجل من بني إسرائيل نجار

IBNHISHAM:v1p580#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p580#2/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p580#2/r2.claim: The Prophet was not present when they disputed over Mary; God's disclosure of concealed knowledge confirms his prophethood and proves the case against them.
IBNHISHAM:v1p580#2/r2.anchor: أي ما كنت معهم إذ يختصمون فيها. يخبره بخفي ما كتموا منه من العلم عندهم، لتحقيق نبوته

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says they cast lots to decide who would care for Mary, and Zechariah won the lot.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p121#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ إذ يلقون أقلامهم ﴾ قال تساهموا على مريم أيهم يكفلها فقرعهم زكريا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r1.claim: Qalam is the familiar writing implement, plural aqlam, and also an arrow used for drawing lots; it is linked to trimming or sharpening, or alternatively to qalamah, a thin plant and a nail clipping, with the verb meaning to pare and smooth nails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r1.anchor: القلم: معروف وهو الذي يكتب به، وجمعه أقلام ويقع على السهم الذي يقترع به

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r2.speaker: زهير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r2.claim: Zuhayr's line about a lion whose claws have not been trimmed illustrates the sense of qalam as cutting or paring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r2.anchor: زهير: لدى أسد شاكي السلاح مقذف ... له لبد أظفاره لم تقلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r3.claim: A later poet compares the crescent to a nail clipping, illustrating qalamah as what falls when a nail is pared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r3.anchor: يشبه بالهلال وذاك نقص ... قلامة ظفره شبه الهلال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r4.claim: Wahy is secretly conveying a meaning into the mind; it may come by angel to a messenger, by inspiration as with the bee, by gesture, or through writing, as in Zuhayr's line about verses preserved like revelation in stone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p143/r4.anchor: الوحي: إلقاء المعنى في النفس في خفاء، فقد يكون بالملك للرسل وبالإلهام كقوله: وأوحى ربك إلى النحل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r1.claim: Al-waḥy can mean the Book; a cited poetic line supports this usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r1.anchor: والوحي: الكتاب قال: فمدافع الريان عري رسمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r2.claim: Another account treats waḥy as a collective of waḥy; the verb occurs as awḥā or waḥā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p144/r2.anchor: وقيل: الوحي جمع: وحي، وأما الفعل فيقال أوحى ووحى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r7.claim: “That” points to the stories of ʿImrān's wife, Mary, Zechariah, and John.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r7.anchor: الإشارة إلى ما تقدم من قصص امرأة عمران، وبنتها مريم، وزكريا، ويحيى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r8.claim: These stories reached Muhammad through revelation: he neither studied books nor associated with a knower of them, and came from an unlettered people.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r8.anchor: والمعنى: أن هذه القصص وصولها إليك من جهة الوحي إذ لست ممن دارس الكتب، ولا صحب من يعرف ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r9.claim: Abū Ḥayyān links the claim to 11:49 and notes that Sūrat Hūd gives the ancient story of Noah more fully than other accounts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r9.anchor: كما قال في الآية الأخرى، وقد ذكر قصة أبعد الناس زمانا من زمانه، صلى الله عليه وسلم، وهو نوح عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r10.claim: The disclosure proves Muhammad's prophethood: he reported unseen matters only a witness, reader of earlier books, or recipient of revelation could know; the first two routes are excluded, leaving revelation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p149/r10.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على نبوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذ أخبر بغيوب لم يطلع عليها إلا من شاهدها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r1.claim: The address in dhālika and ilayka is to the Prophet; the preferred parsing makes dhālika the subject and min anbāʾ al-ghayb its predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r1.anchor: والكاف في: ذلك، و: إليك، خطاب للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، والأحسن في الإعراب أن يكون:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers نوحيه as a new sentence with its pronoun referring to the unseen: God continually reveals and teaches the unseen, including future stories.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r2.anchor: وأن يكون: نوحيه، جملة مستأنفة، ويكون الضمير في: نوحيه، عائدا على الغيب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r3.claim: The present tense suits an ongoing practice of revelation; referring the pronoun instead to dhālika would force a completed past sense and be less apt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r3.anchor: ولذلك أتى بالمضارع، ويكون أكثر فائدة من عوده على: ذلك، إذ يشتمل ما تقدم من القصص وغيرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r4.claim: Other parses make نوحيه the predicate of dhālika, with min anbāʾ either circumstantial from its pronoun or attached to the verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r4.anchor: وجوزوا أن يكون: نوحيه، خبرا: لذلك، و: من أنباء، حال من: الهاء، في: نوحيه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r5.claim: The denial of presence establishes that knowledge of the story came from God; the two stories are Mary's and Zechariah's, with Mary primary and Zechariah included incidentally through the guardianship question.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r5.anchor: وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم هذا تقرير وتثبيت أن ما علمه من ذلك إنما هو بوحي من الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r6.claim: Denying eyewitness knowledge while leaving reading or transmission technically open taunts deniers of revelation, who knew Muhammad neither read nor learned reports from transmitters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r6.anchor: ونفي المشاهدة، وإن كانت منتفية بالعلم ولم تنتف القراءة والتلقي، من حفاظ الأنباء على سبيل التهكم بالمنكرين للوحي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān compares the statement with revelations about Moses's absence at the western side and the Mount, and Joseph's brothers conspiring.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r7.anchor: ونظيره في قصة موسى: وما كنت بجانب الغرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r8.claim: Abū Ḥayyān illustrates contextual reference to a place with 100:4, where “there” means the place where the horses stir dust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r8.anchor: كقوله: فأثرن به نقعا أي: بالمكان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r9.claim: The pronoun in ladayhim refers to unnamed disputants inferred from the context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150/r9.anchor: والضمير، في: لديهم، عائد على غير مذكور، بل على ما دل عليه المعنى، أي: وما كنت لدى المتنازعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r1.claim: The governing word for idh is the earlier phrase ladayhim; Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī instead makes kuntu govern it, which Abū Ḥayyān rejects because defective kāna has no event for an adverb to attach to.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r1.anchor: والعامل في: إذ، العامل في: لديهم. وقال أبو علي الفارسي: العامل في: إذ، كنت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r2.claim: The imperfect verb after idh carries past meaning here.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r2.anchor: والمضارع بعد: إذ، في معنى الماضي، أي: إذ ألقوا أقلامهم للاستهام على مريم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r3.claim: The apparent referent of the pens is writing pens.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r4.claim: Some say they were pens used to write the Torah, chosen for the lot as a blessing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة، فاختاروها للقرعة تبركا بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r5.claim: Others identify the pens as azlām, lottery arrows or divining lots.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: الأقلام هنا الأزلام، وهي: القداح، ومعنى الإلقاء هنا الرمي والطرح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r6.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r6.claim: Abū Muslim says disputants wrote their names on arrows and drew one to decide the matter, like lots used to divide a camel carcass.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r6.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: كانت الأمم يكتبون أسماءهم على سهام عند المنازعة، فمن خرج له السهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r7.claim: The verse omits what the pens were thrown into, how the drawing worked, and how Zechariah's pen emerged; Abū Ḥayyān leaves the correct details to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r7.anchor: ولم يذكر في الآية ما الذي ألقوها فيه، ولا كيفية حال الإلقاء، كيف خرج قلم زكريا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r8.claim: Ayyuhum yakfulu is nominative subject and predicate but occupies an object-like slot: it can quote omitted speech, express purpose, or be circumstantial, with the missing verb inferred from yulqūna.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r8.anchor: وارتفع أيهم يكفل مريم على الابتداء والخبر، وهو في موضع نصب إما على الحكاية بقول محذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r9.claim: Jurists cite this verse as evidence that drawing lots is established in law.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r9.anchor: وقد استدل بهذه الآية على إثبات القرعة وهي مسألة فقهية تذكر في علم الفقه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r10.claim: The later dispute concerns Mary and may either be the lot-drawing itself or another dispute afterward; either way it emphasizes their eagerness to care for her.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v3p150#2/r10.anchor: وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون أي: بسبب مريم، ويحتمل أن يكون هذا الاختصام هو الاقتراع

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r1.claim: That points back to the remarkable preceding accounts, which are hidden from the Prophet and his people and knowable only through revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم ذكره من تلك الاخبار البديعة الشأن المرتقية من الغرابة إلى أعلى مكان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r2.claim: That is the subject, with from the unseen reports as its predicate; the sentence is grammatically independent.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r2.anchor: وهو مبتدأ خبره قوله تعالى : ( من أنبآء الغيب ( أي من أخبار ما غاب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r3.claim: The clause from the unseen reports is an independent sentence with no grammatical position.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r3.anchor: والجملة مستأنفة لا محل لها من الاعراب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r4.claim: Revelation is imparting meaning secretly; the word can also mean an angel's delivery to prophets or inspiration.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r4.anchor: إلقاء المعنى إلى الغير على وجه خفي ويكون بمعنى إرسال الملك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r5.claim: Most take its pronoun to refer to that; al-Alusi prefers the unseen, which includes both previously told and untold stories.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r5.anchor: عائد إلى ذلك في المشهور واستحسن عوده إلى الغيب

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r6.claim: An alternate parsing makes this clause the predicate, with from the unseen reports attached to the verb or circumstantial from its object; some make it circumstantial from the subject.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r6.anchor: وجوز أن تكون هذه الجملة خبرا عن المبتدأ قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r7.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r7.claim: Abu al-Baqa proposes an omitted subject meaning the matter is that, with the prepositional phrase circumstantial; al-Alusi rejects this as unworthy of the divine speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r7.anchor: التقدير الامر ( ذلك ) فيكون ( ذلك ) خبرا لمبتدأ محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
