ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r8.speaker: قوم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r8.claim: Some take the present tense to signal that revelation was still continuing.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r8.anchor: وصيغة الاستقبال عند قوم للإيذان بأن الوحي لم ينقطع بعد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r9.claim: The unstated pronoun means those disputing over Mary, inferred from the context.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r9.anchor: أي عند المتنازعين فالضمير عائد إلى غير مذكور دل عليه المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r10.claim: The denial of the Prophet's presence establishes that his account came by revelation: reason and prior reading or hearing could not supply it, leaving only impossible eyewitnessing.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r10.anchor: تحقيق كون الاخبار بما ذكر عن وحي على سبيل التهكم بمنكريه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r11.claim: Mary's story is foregrounded although Zakariya's story was also revealed, because Mary is the primary subject; Zakariya's account enters incidentally and is partly implied by the mention of her caretaker.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r11.anchor: هي المقصودة بالاخبار أولا وإنما جاءت القصة الأخرى على سبيل الاستطراد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r12.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r12.claim: Qatada says the sentence marvels at the people's eagerness to take responsibility for Mary and reinforces her selection.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r12.anchor: وروى عن قتادة أن المقصود من هذه الجملة تعجيب الله سبحانه نبيه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r13.claim: Al-Alusi finds Qatada's reading strained because it separates emphasis from what is emphasized, yet prefers it to the alternative explanation.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r13.anchor: ويبعد هذا الفصل بين المؤكد والمؤكد ومع هذا هو أولى مما قيل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r14.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r14.claim: An alternative says the verse marvels that people shirked Mary's care because of their hardship and need until Zakariya became her excellent guardian; al-Alusi nearly rejects this as unsound in reason and transmission.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r14.anchor: إن المقصود منها التعجيب من تدافعهم لكفالتها لشدة الحال ومزيد الحاجة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r15.claim: Whichever purpose is adopted, denying eyewitnessing poses no problem because its impossibility is evident to everyone.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r15.anchor: لا يشكل نفي المشاهدة مع ظهور انتقائها عند كل أحد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r16.claim: The pens are cast or thrown for drawing lots; qalam is the plural of pen.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r16.anchor: يرمونها ويطرحونها للاقتراع و الاقلام جمع قلم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r17.claim: The lots used their Torah-writing pens, chosen for the blessing associated with them.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r17.anchor: وهي التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة واختاروها تبركا بها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r18.speaker: الكازروني
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r18.claim: Others say the lots were arrows or divining shafts; al-Kazruni reports that they were made of copper.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r18.anchor: وقيل : هي السهام من النشاب وهي القداح وحكى الكازروني أنها كانت من نحاس

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r19.claim: Qalam derives from a root meaning to cut, as in a nail clipping.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r19.anchor: وهي مأخوذة من القلم بمعنى القطع ومنه قلامة الظفر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r20.speaker: الباقر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r20.claim: Al-Baqir says the number of lots was six; the source notes disagreement about their number.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r20.anchor: وفي عدة الأقلام خلاف وعن الباقر أنها كانت ستة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r21.claim: The temporal clause is governed by the existential construction operating in with them.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r21.anchor: والظرف معمول للاستقرار العامل في ( لديهم ) وجعله ظرفا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r22.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r22.claim: Abu al-Baqa's alternative attachment of the time phrase to كان is rejected.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r22.anchor: وجعله ظرفا لكان كما قال أبو البقاء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r23.claim: Who will care for Mary continues the preceding construction; treating it as a fresh direct question corrupts the meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r23.anchor: من تتمة الكلام الأول وجعله ابتداء استفهام مفسد للمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r24.speaker: ابن الحاجب وابن مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r24.claim: One proposed ellipsis is they look to see who will care for Mary; looking can govern an interrogative like a verb of cognition, as Ibn al-Hajib and Ibn Malik state.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r24.anchor: أن يقدر ينظرون ( أيهم يكفل ) وحيث كان النظر مما يؤدي

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r25.claim: A second ellipsis supplies they may know who will care for Mary; the clause is purposive, although casting lots is only an indirect cause and observing which pen rises is the immediate cause.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r25.anchor: أن يقدر ليعلموا ( أيهم يكفل ) وعلى الأول الجملة حال مما قبلها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r26.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r26.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r26.claim: A third proposal supplies they say or so they say; critics find it purposeless, while its defenders understand saying as identifying or judging who will care for her.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r26.anchor: أن يقدر يقولون أو ليقولوا ( أيهم ) واعترض بأنه لا فائدة يعتد بها

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r27.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r27.speaker: السكاكي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r27.claim: Al-Sakkaki supplies they look so they may know, perhaps to preserve both the sense and wording; either verb of looking or knowing could suffice.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r27.anchor: والسكاكي يقدر ههنا ينظرون ليعلموا ولعل ذلك لمراعاة المعنى واللفظ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r28.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r28.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r28.claim: Some exacting scholars supply no omitted verb and make who will care for Mary an appositive to the plural pronoun, a strained analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p158/r28.anchor: وبعض المحققين لم يقدر شيئا أصلا وجعل ( أيهم ) بدلا عن ضمير الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r1.claim: The dispute concerned competing over Mary's guardianship; one view places it after the lot drawing and another before it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r1.anchor: في شأنها تنافسا على كفالتها وكان هذا الاختصام بعد الاقتراع في رأي وقبله في آخر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r2.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r2.claim: Repeating that the Prophet was not present makes each absence an independent proof of prophethood; the altered order of events in the second account strengthens the point.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r2.anchor: للايذان بأن كل واحد من عدم الحضور عند الإلقاء وعدم الحضور عند الاختصام مستقل بالشهادة على نبوته

ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r3.claim: The well-known, relied-upon view places the drawing of lots when Mary was born and her mother brought her to the church; another weak view places it when grown Mary became difficult for Zakariya to raise, and a still weaker view says it happened twice.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r3.anchor: أحدهما وهو المشهور المعول عليه أنه كان حين ولادتها وحمل أمها لها إلى الكنيسة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r4.claim: The verse shows that drawing lots can help determine disputed rights.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r4.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دلالة على أن القرعة لها دخل في تمييز الحقوق

ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r5.speaker: الصادق
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r5.claim: Al-Sadiq says that people who cast lots while entrusting the matter to God see the rightful claimant's lot succeed, and cites the lot cast by Jonah.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r5.anchor: وروى عن الصادق رضى الله تعالى عنه أنه قال

ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r6.speaker: الباقر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r6.claim: Al-Baqir says Mary daughter of Imran was the first person against whom lots were cast, citing this verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p159/r6.anchor: وقال الباقر رضي الله تعالى عنه : أول من سوهم عليه مريم بنت عمران

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r1.claim: The demonstrative refers to the accounts just given of Zakariya, Yahya, Mary, and Jesus.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r1.anchor: {ذلك} الذي ذكرت من حديث زكريا ويحيى ومريم وعيسى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r2.claim: These are reports of the unseen that God reveals to Muhammad.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r3.claim: The pronoun in the revelation verb refers back to dhalika, which accounts for its masculine form.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r3.anchor: رد الكناية إلى ذلك فلذلك ذكره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r4.claim: Their pens were casting lots in water to decide who would care for Mary.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r5.claim: The question is which person would take Mary in, raise her, and care for her.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r6.claim: The dispute among them concerned who would have custody of Mary.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v2p38/r6.anchor: وما كنت لديهم إذ يختصمون} في كفالتها

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r1.claim: The previously recounted stories are unseen events unknown except through revelation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r1.anchor: أي ما ذكرنا من القصص من الغيوب التي لم تعرفها إلا بالوحي

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r2.claim: The pens are drawing lots; another view says they cast the pens with which they wrote the Torah, seeking blessing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r2.anchor: أقداحهم للاقتراع. وقيل اقترعوا بأقلامهم التى كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة تبركا

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r3.claim: The passage establishes revelation and mocks its deniers: the means of knowing witnessed or heard events are clear, leaving direct observation as the only alleged alternative, which no sensible person would claim.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r3.anchor: والمراد تقرير كونه وحيا على سبيل التهكم بمنكريه، فإن طريق معرفة الوقائع المشاهدة والسماع وعدم السماع معلوم لا شبهة فيه عندهم فبقي أن يكون الإتهام باحتمال العيان ولا يظن به عاقل

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r4.claim: “Which of them would care for Maryam?” depends on an omitted phrase indicated by “casting lots”: either they cast to learn who would care for her or said those words.
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r4.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف دل عليه { يلقون أقلمهم } أي يلقونها

BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:3:44/r5.claim: Their dispute was competition over who would be Maryam’s guardian.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r1.claim: These exact, remarkable reports of hidden Israelite history should awaken listeners and prove the Prophet truthful, since he had no contact with scholars or access to such knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r1.anchor: الغريبة المحررة العجيبة التي لا يعرفها على وجهها إلا الحذاق من علماء بني إسرائيل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r2.claim: ذلك points to the elevated, truthful, and finely ordered discourse; نوحيه describes revelation being renewed in accounts like this.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r2.anchor: أي الخطاب العلي المقام الصادق المرام البديع النظام

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r3.claim: The statement that the Prophet was not present may be read as a circumstantial clause: while you were not with them.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r3.anchor: أن تكون الجملة حالا تقديرها : { و } الحال أنك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r4.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r4.claim: لدى denotes presence with something of elevated status.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r4.anchor: لدى هي عند حاضرة لرفعة ذلك الشيء الذي ينبأ به عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r5.claim: The pens were cast for drawing lots; a pen is a visible trace that points to what lies beyond it.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r5.anchor: جمع قلم , وهو مظهر الآثار المنبئة عما وراءها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r6.claim: They drew lots to decide who would foster Mary, competing for the honor because of the distinction God had granted her.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r6.anchor: أي يحضنها ويربيها تنافسا في أمرها لما شرفها الله تعالى به

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r7.claim: The Prophet had neither witnessed their dispute nor learned its details from people; his known distance from scholars and literary training leaves revelation as the source.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r7.anchor: ومن الواضح الجلي أن بعد نسبتك إلى التعلم من البشر كبعد نسبتك إلى الحضور بينهم في ذلك الوقت

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r8.claim: The reminder appears near the middle of the story so listeners recall what preceded it and attend to what follows.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r8.anchor: وجعل هذا التنبيه في نحو وسط هذا القصص ليكون السامع على ذكر مما مضى ويلقي السمع

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r9.claim: The notice follows Mary’s opening story to emphasize that she is central to the account, which answers the Christians of Najran.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r9.anchor: وجعله بعد الافتتاح بقصة مريم عليها السلام تنبيها على عظم شأنها وأنها المقصودة بالذات للرد على وفد نصارى نجران

BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r10.claim: The cast lots are obscure even to most scriptural experts; their pens also foreshadow the announcement of one who will be taught the Book.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p87/r10.anchor: واختصامهم في كفالتها لخفائه إلى على خواص أهل الكتاب

DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r9.claim: The scholars drew lots three times with their pens; after a boy first drew Zachariah's pen, they rejected that method and agreed to cast the pens in flowing water, awarding custody to the pen that went with the current and rose.
DURR-FULL:v2p180#2/r9.anchor: فقرعوا ثلاث مرات بأقلامهم التي كانوا يكتبون بها الوحي {أيهم يكفل مريم}

DURR-FULL:v2p184/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عباس وناس من الصحابة
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r9.claim: The Torah scribes used lots to choose who would teach a consecrated person; Zachariah was then their best scholar and argued for Mary because her maternal aunt was his wife.
DURR-FULL:v2p184/r9.anchor: عن ابن مسعود وابن عباس وناس من الصحابة إن الذين كانوا يكتبون التوراة

DURR-FULL:v2p195/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r8.claim: Qatada says the address 'you were not with them' refers to Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r8.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {وما كنت لديهم} يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v2p195/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says the prayer-place community cast lots with their pens to decide who would care for Mary; God tells Muhammad he was absent from their drawing and dispute.
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وما كنت لديهم إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم} قال

DURR-FULL:v2p195/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r10.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r10.claim: Ikrima says they cast their pens into water; Zachariah's pen rose against the current and he won Mary's care.
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r10.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله {إذ يلقون أقلامهم أيهم يكفل مريم} قال: ألقوا أقلامهم في الماء

DURR-FULL:v2p195/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r11.speaker: الربيع
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r11.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says aqalam refers to sticks thrown toward the water's current; Zachariah's stick faced the current and won the lot.
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r11.anchor: عن الربيع قال: ألقوا أقلامهم يقال: عصيهم تلقاء جرية الماء

DURR-FULL:v2p195/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r12.speaker: ابن جريج
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r12.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the pens as those used to write the Torah.
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r12.anchor: عن ابن جريج قال {أقلامهم} قال: التي يكتبون بها التوراة

DURR-FULL:v2p195/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r13.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r13.claim: Mujahid agrees that the pens were used to write the Torah.

DURR-FULL:v2p195/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r14.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v2p195/r14.claim: Ata explains the pens as divining arrows used for drawing lots.

DURR-FULL:v2p196/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r1.claim: God tells Muhammad that the account of Zechariah, John, and Mary is unseen news revealed to him, although he was not present when they cast lots over Mary's care.
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r1.anchor: يقول الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم {ذلك من أنباء الغيب نوحيه إليك} يعني بالخبر {الغيب} في قصة زكريا

DURR-FULL:v2p196/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r2.claim: He glosses al-ghayb here as the report concerning Zechariah, John, and Mary.
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r2.anchor: يعني بالخبر {الغيب} في قصة زكريا ويحيى ومريم

DURR-FULL:v2p196/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r3.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r3.claim: He explains the phrase as meaning that Muhammad was not among them or at their side.
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r3.anchor: {وما كنت لديهم} يعني عندهم {إذ يلقون أقلامهم}

DURR-FULL:v2p196/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r8.speaker: وهب
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r8.claim: Wahb says Mary's fellow consecrated servant was her cousin Joseph, who served and spoke with her from behind the veil; he first noticed her pregnancy and was troubled, not knowing its cause.
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r8.anchor: وأخرج اسحق بن بشر وابن عساكر عن وهب قال: لما استقر حمل مريم وبشرها جبريل وثقت بكرامة الله

DURR-FULL:v2p196/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r9.speaker: وهب
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r9.claim: Wahb recounts that Mary and Joseph fetched water together and returned to the church while angels brought Mary the glad tidings that God had chosen and purified her; Joseph wondered at what he heard.
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r9.anchor: وكانت مريم إذا نفذ ماؤها وماء يوسف أخذا قلتيهما ثم انطلقا إلى المفازة التي فيها الماء

DURR-FULL:v2p196/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r10.speaker: وهب
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r10.claim: When Mary's pregnancy became evident, Joseph recalled her purification, her mother's prayer, the angels' words, Zechariah's protection, and the absence of Satan; seeing her changing color and swelling, he asked whether conception could occur without seed, and she said yes.
DURR-FULL:v2p196/r10.anchor: فلما استبان ليوسف حمل مريم وقع في نفسه من أمرها حتى كاد أن يفتتن

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r1.claim: Abū Mālik glosses anbāʾ as accounts or reports.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك قوله : انباء يعني احاديث .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r2.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r2.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says the Prophet's delivery of these unseen reports to the people is evidence of his prophethood and an argument against them.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r2.anchor: محمد بن اسحاق قوله : ذلك من انباء الغيب نوحيه اليك ثم قد جئتهم به

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq explains the phrase as meaning that Muhammad was neither present with them nor aware of their affairs.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r3.anchor: محمد بن اسحاق وما كنت لديهم يقول : ما حضرت ولا عنيت .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās recounts that when Mary was placed in the mosque, its worshippers cast lots with their pens to decide who would care for her.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس : اذ يلقون اقلامهم ايهم يكفل مريم وان مريم لما وضعت في المسجد اقترغ غليها اهل المصلى

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says they cast lots over who would care for Mary and Zachariah won.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r5.anchor: عن قتادة : اذ يلقون اقلامهم قال : تساهموا على مريم ايهم يكفلها فقرعهم زكريا .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد، الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk are also reported to say that they drew lots with their pens.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r6.anchor: روى عن مجاهد . 2 والضحاك قالا : استهموا باقلامهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r7.speaker: عكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r7.claim: ʿIkrima says the pens were thrown into water and swept along, while Zachariah's pen rose against the current and prevailed, winning him Mary's care.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r7.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله : اذ يلقون اقلامهم قال : القوا اقلامهم في الماء فذهبت مع الجرية ، وصعد قلم زكريا يغلب الجرية

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r8.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r8.claim: ʿAṭāʾ, in Ibn Jurayj's report, glosses the pens as lots or arrows used for drawing lots.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن جريج قال عطاء : يعني اقلامهم : قداحهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r9.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r9.claim: ʿAṭāʾ also says these were the pens with which they wrote the Torah.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r9.anchor: وعن عطاء ابن جريج قال : فالقوا اقلامهم التي يكتبون بها التوراة .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r10.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r10.claim: Al-Rabīʿ gives a second gloss for the pens: their staffs.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p648#2/r10.anchor: عن الربيع قوله : اقلامهم يقول : عصيهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r1.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r1.claim: Al-Rabīʿ relates that they threw their staffs toward the water current; Zachariah's staff faced the current and beat theirs, so he took Mary.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r1.anchor: عن الربيع قوله : ايهم يكفل مريم فقال الربيع : القو اقلامهم . القوها تلقاء جرية الماء ، فاستقبلت عصى زكريا جرية الماء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r2.speaker: أبو مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r2.claim: Abū Mālik glosses ladayhim as being in their presence or with them.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r2.anchor: عن أبي مالك قوله : لديهم يعني : عندهم .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq explains that Muhammad was not with them.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r3.anchor: قال محمد بن اسحاق وما كنت لديهم اي ما كنت معهم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r4.claim: Qatāda says Mary was the daughter of their imam and chief; the Israelites disputed over her care and drew lots.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r4.anchor: عن قتادة يعني قوله : وما كنت لديهم اذ يختصمون قال : كانت ابنة امامهم وسيدهم ، فتشاح عليها بنو اسرائيل فاقترعوا بها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r5.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says God revealed to Muhammad what the disputants had concealed of their knowledge, confirming his prophethood and establishing an argument against them.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p650/r5.anchor: قال محمد ابن اسحاق : وما كنت لديهم اذ يختصمون اي ما كنت معهم اذ يختصون فيها ، يخبره يخفي ما كتموا منه من العلم عندهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r1.claim: Dhālika points to the preceding stories; anbāʾ means reports, and al-ghayb is what lies beyond human perception.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r1.anchor: والإشارة ب ذلك إلى ما تقدم ذكره من القصص، والأنباء الأخبار، والغيب ما غاب عن مدارك الإنسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r2.claim: Waḥy is secretly placing meaning in the soul; it may occur through an angel, inspiration, a gesture, or writing. Arabic uses both awḥā and waḥy.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r2.anchor: ونوحيه معناه نلقيه في نفسك في خفاء، وحد الوحي إلقاء المعنى في النفس في خفاء، ثم تختلف أنواعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r3.speaker: كعب بن زهير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r3.claim: Kaʿb ibn Zuhayr compares enduring poems inscribed in hard stone to the persistence of waḥy; his line witnesses the term's Arabic usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r3.anchor: كما قال كعب بن زهير: [الطويل] أتى العجم والآفاق منه قصائد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r4.claim: The account proves Muḥammad's prophethood: he conveyed unseen events known by eyewitnesses or scripture, though he was unlettered among an unlettered people, so God must have taught him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r4.anchor: وفي هذه الآية بيان لنبوة محمد عليه السلام، إذ جاءهم بغيوب لا يعلمها إلا من شاهدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r6.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r6.claim: Most scholars say the lot was cast to win custody of Maryam, with the caretakers competing for her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r6.anchor: وجمهور العلماء على أنه استهام لأخذها والمنافسة فيها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r7.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r7.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says they cast lots during famine to transfer the cost of supporting her.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r7.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: إنما كان استهامهم حين نالتهم المجاعة دفعا منها لتحمل مؤونتها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r8.claim: Yakhtaṣimūn means they exchanged words aloud while debating her case.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r8.anchor: ويختصمون معناه يتراجعون القول الجهير في أمرها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r9.claim: Drawing lots is a Sunnah, evidenced by the Prophet's lots among his wives when travelling and his statement about people vying for the first prayer row.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r9.anchor: وفي هذه الآية استعمال القرعة والقرعة سنة، وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سافر أقرع بين نسائه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r10.speaker: جمهور الأمة; بعض أهل العلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r10.claim: Most Muslims permit lots when a fair allocation is needed; a dissenting minority calls them gambling, though the lot settles a division acceptable by consent.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r10.anchor: وجمهور الأمة على تجويز القرعة إلا من شذ فظنها قمارا، وهذا كله فيما يصلح التراضي بكونه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r11.speaker: جمهور العلماء; أبو حنيفة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r11.claim: For dividing emancipation among slaves within a bequest's one-third, most permit lots but Abū Ḥanīfah forbids them; a report says the Prophet drew lots among six slaves, freeing two and retaining four.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p434#3/r11.anchor: وأما حيث لا يجوز التراضي كعتق العبيد في ثلث ميت فجوزها الجمهور ومنعها أبو حنيفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p435/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p435/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p435/r1.claim: Ayyuhum yakfulu Maryam is an initial subject and predicate governed in the accusative by an omitted verb meaning “they consider which one will care for her.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p435/r1.anchor: أيهم يكفل مريم ابتداء وخبر في موضع نصب بالفعل الذي تقديره، ينظرون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p435/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p435/r5.speaker: المتأولون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p435/r5.claim: Commentators disagree whether “the angels” refers to Gabriel alone or a group; Ibn ʿAṭiyya directs readers to his earlier discussion of 3:39.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p435/r5.anchor: واختلف المتأولون هل الملائكة هنا عبارة عن جبريل وحده أو عن جماعة من الملائكة؟

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r1.claim: That points to the preceding accounts of Zakariya, Yahya, Jesus, and Mary; anbāʾ are reports and ghayb is what is hidden from you.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r2.claim: Ibn Qutayba uses waḥy broadly for anything that conveys a message through speech, writing, gesture, or correspondence.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r2.anchor: والوحي كل شيء دللت به من كلام أو كتاب أو إشارة أو رسالة قاله ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن جبير، السدي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r3.claim: One view identifies the pens as writing implements.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r3.anchor: وفي الأقلام ثلاثة أقوال أحدها أنها التي يكتب بها قاله ابن عباس وابن جبير والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r4.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r4.claim: A second view identifies the pens as staffs.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r4.anchor: والثاني أنها العصي قاله الربيع بن أنس والثالث أنها القداح وهو اختيار ابن قتيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r5.claim: A third, preferred view takes them as marked arrows used for drawing lots.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r5.anchor: والثالث أنها القداح وهو اختيار ابن قتيبة وكذلك قال الزجاج هي قداح جعلوا عليها علامات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r6.speaker: ابن قتيبة، الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r6.claim: Qalam is related to qalama, to cut or sharpen something bit by bit; a writing pen is called a qalam because it is repeatedly sharpened, as are clipped nails.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r6.anchor: قيل للسهم القلم لأنه يقلم أي يبرى وكل ما قطعت منه شيئا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r7.claim: The question means determining which person should have custody of Mary, that is, guarantee and undertake her care.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r7.anchor: لينظروا أيهم تجب له كفالة مريم وهو الضمان للقيام بأمرها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r8.claim: Ladayhim means “with them” or “in their presence.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p388#2/r8.anchor: عندهم وقد سبق شرح كفالتهم لها آنفا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r4.claim: God recounts the hidden events to Muhammad; the Prophet was not physically present to witness them, but revelation showed them to him as if he had been there.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r4.anchor: ما كنت عندهم يا محمد فتخبرهم (4) عنهم معاينة عما جرى، بل أطلعك الله على ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r5.claim: The people cast lots with their pens to decide who would care for Mary because they wanted the reward of looking after her.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r5.anchor: حين اقترعوا في شأن مريم أيهم يكفلها، وذلك لرغبتهم في الأجر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r6.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Ikrima that Mary’s mother brought her as a vowed offering to the temple custodians, who objected that she was the daughter of their prayer leader Imran; Zakariyya requested her because her maternal aunt was his wife, but they disputed custody.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة -وأبي بكر، عن عكرمة-قال: ثم خرجت بها -يعني أم مريم بمريم-تحملها في خرقها إلى بني الكاهن بن هارون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r7.speaker: عكرمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r7.claim: In Ikrima’s account, they cast the pens used to write the Torah to settle custody, and Zakariyya won the lot and became Mary’s guardian.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r7.anchor: فذلك حين اقترعوا بأقلامهم عليها (10) التي يكتبون بها التوراة، فقرعهم زكريا، فكفلها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r8.speaker: عكرمة، والسدي، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r8.claim: Ikrima, al-Suddi, Qatada, al-Rabi ibn Anas, and others say the contestants cast pens into the Jordan; the current carried all away except Zakariyya’s, which some say moved upstream, so he won custody.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r8.anchor: وقد ذكر عكرمة أيضا، والسدي، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس، وغير واحد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r9.claim: The account describes Zakariyya as their chief, master, scholar, imam, and prophet.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v2p42/r9.anchor: وكان مع ذلك كبيرهم وسيدهم، وعالمهم وإمامهم ونبيهم صلوات الله وسلامه عليه سائر النبيين

JISHUMI:v2p1162/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r2.claim: Anbāʾ means reports; its singular is nabaʾ.

JISHUMI:v2p1162/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r3.claim: Waḥy is conveying a meaning secretly; the term also applies to inspiration and to sending a message.
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r3.anchor: والإيحاء: إلقاء المعنى إلى غيره على وجه يخفى، ثم يسمى الإلهام وحيا، والإرسال وحيا

JISHUMI:v2p1162/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r4.claim: Qalam is related to cutting: it can mean clipping a nail, the clipped fragment, or a pen, named for its sharpened, cut tip.
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r4.anchor: والقلم: قص الظفر، والقلامة: ما يقطع منه، والقلم: واحد الأقلام سمي به لأنه يبرى

JISHUMI:v2p1162/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r5.claim: The unseen is what is absent from the senses, opposite what is present.
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r5.anchor: والغائب: ما غاب عن الحواس، ونقيضه الحاضر

JISHUMI:v2p1162/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r8.claim: The pronoun in nūḥīhi refers back to dhālika: that is what God reveals to the Prophet.
JISHUMI:v2p1162/r8.anchor: رد على (ذلك)؛ أي: يوحي ذلك إليك

JISHUMI:v2p1163/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r5.claim: Dhālika refers to the preceding accounts of Zachariah, Yahya, and Jesus; anbāʾ al-ghayb means reports of the unseen, and nūḥīhi means conveying them for Muhammad to know.
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r5.anchor: ذلك يعني ما تقدم ذكره من حديث زكريا ويحيى وعيسى

JISHUMI:v2p1163/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r6.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r6.claim: One account says they were writing the Torah and threw their pens into water to determine who would care for Mary; another takes the pens as arrows or lots, with an implied purpose of finding whose lot wins.
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r6.anchor: قيل: كانوا يكتبون التوراة، فألقوا الأقلام التي كانت بأيديهم في الماء أيهم يكفل مريم

JISHUMI:v2p1163/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r7.speaker: قتادة
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r7.claim: Qatāda says the account marvels at their eagerness to care for Mary because of her merit; another view marvels that they resisted during a severe crisis until Zachariah became her guardian.
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r7.anchor: من حرصهم على كفالتها لفضلها عن قتادة قال: تشاح القوم عليها

JISHUMI:v2p1163/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r8.speaker: الربيع
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r8.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the lots went into flowing water: Zachariah's pen moved upstream while others went downstream; Ibn Isḥāq and al-Suddī report variants where his pen rose or stood above theirs.
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r8.anchor: عن الربيع، وقيل: ارتفع قلمه فوق الماء وانحدرت أقلامهم ورسبت في النهر

JISHUMI:v2p1163/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r9.claim: Muhammad was not present when they disputed Mary's guardianship; their dispute had grown into an argument.
JISHUMI:v2p1163/r9.anchor: وما كنت يا محمد لديهم عندهم إذ يختصمون في تكفل مريم، وفيه تنبيه على أن التشاح بينهم بلغ إلى حد الخصومة

JISHUMI:v2p1164/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1164/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1164/r5.claim: The report is a miracle proving Muhammad's prophethood: he could not have learned it by witnessing events, reading a book, or instruction, so it must have come by revelation.
JISHUMI:v2p1164/r5.anchor: وقد بطلت الأوجه الثلاثة، فثبت أنه بوحي، وأنه معجزة له

JISHUMI:v2p1164/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v2p1164/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v2p1164/r6.claim: The account shows that drawing lots can distinguish competing rights.
JISHUMI:v2p1164/r6.anchor: وتدل على أن للقرعة مدخلا في تميز الحقوق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r1.claim: Dhālika points to the preceding accounts of Zakariyyā, Yaḥyā, Mary, and Jesus: these unseen events were known to the Prophet only through revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r1.anchor: اشارة إلى ما سبق من نبإ زكريا ويحيى ومريم وعيسى عليهم السلام يعني ان ذلك من الغيوب التى لم تعرفها الا بالوحي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r2.claim: The denial singles out eyewitnessing because the opponents knew the Prophet had neither listened to tellers nor read their books; denying that he witnessed it sarcastically challenges those who rejected revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r2.anchor: كان معلوما عندهم علما يقينا انه ليس من اهل السماع والقراءة وكانوا منكرين للوحي فلم يبق الا المشاهدة وهي في غاية الاستبعاد والاستحالة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r3.claim: He parallels this denial of presence with the statements about not being at the western side, Mount, or when Joseph’s brothers plotted.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r4.claim: Aqlām may mean the lots or arrow-shafts they cast into the river to decide who would care for Mary.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r4.anchor: أزلامهم وهي قداحهم التى طرحوها في النهر مقترعين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r5.claim: Alternatively, they were the pens used to write the Torah, chosen for the lot as an act of seeking blessing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#2/r5.anchor: وقيل هي الأقلام التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة اختاروها للقرعة تبركا بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#3/r1.claim: They were competing and disputing over who would take responsibility for Mary.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#3/r1.anchor: في شأنها تنافسا في التكفل بها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#3/r2.claim: Ayyuhum yakful may depend on an implied phrase prompted by yalqūna aqlāmahum: they cast the pens to see, learn, or say who would care for her.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p390#3/r2.anchor: بمحذوف دل عليه يلقون أقلامهم كانه قيل يلقونها ينظرون أيهم يكفل أو ليعلموا أو يقولون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p391/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p391/r16.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p391/r16.claim: 'That' refers to the glad tidings about the Messiah.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p391/r16.anchor: يعني ما كان من البشرى بالمسيح .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p391/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p391/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p391/r17.claim: Wahy is conveying meaning: to prophets by revelation, to bees by inspiration, and between people by gesture; the Qur'anic example is 19:11, and al-Ajjaj is cited.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p391/r17.anchor: وأصل الوحي إلقاء المعنى إلى صاحبه , والوحي إلى الرسل الإلقاء بالإنزال , وإلى النحل بالإلهام

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r1.claim: The line by al-Ajjaj, 'the resting-place signaled to her, and she settled,' illustrates the use of wahy to convey meaning.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ikrima, al-Hasan, and al-Rabi say the people disputed custody because each sought Mary; they cast lots by throwing pens into flowing water, and Zakariya won when his staff moved upstream while theirs flowed down.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r2.anchor: فقرعهم زكريا , وهو معنى قوله تعالى : { وكفلها } وهذا قول ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r3.speaker: سعيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r3.claim: Sa'id says Zakariya had already taken Mary without lots, but later asked others to assume her care during hardship; they resisted, so he cast lots with them and won.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p393/r3.anchor: فأقرع بينهم وبين نفسه فخرجت القرعة له , وهذا قول سعيد

MUJAHID:v1p127#2/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p127#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p127#2/r2.claim: Those casting lots for Mary's guardianship were Zachariah and his companions, using their pens after she had been brought to them.
MUJAHID:v1p127#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ إذ يلقون أقلامهم ﴾ يعني زكريا وأصحابه استهموا بأقلامهم على مريم حين دلت عليهم

MUQATIL:3:44/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:44/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:44/r1.claim: These events are unseen news revealed by God to Muhammad, who was not present when the people cast lots or disputed over Mary.
MUQATIL:3:44/r1.anchor: يعنى حديثا من الغيب لم تشهده يا محمد

MUQATIL:3:44/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:3:44/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:3:44/r2.claim: They cast lots to decide who would take Mary into his care and later disputed over her guardianship.
MUQATIL:3:44/r2.anchor: فى القرعة، { أيهم يكفل مريم } ، يعنى يضم مريم إلى نفسه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r1.claim: «That» points to the accounts of Ḥanna, Zechariah, John, and Mary.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى ما سبق من قصة حنة وزكريا ويحيى ومريم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r2.claim: These were matters of the unseen that the Prophet knew only through revelation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r2.anchor: يعنى أن ذلك من الغيوب التى لم تعرفها إلا بالوحى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r3.claim: The pens may be divination arrows cast into the river to draw lots, or the pens used to write the Torah, chosen for the lot as a blessing.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r3.anchor: أزلامهم وهى قداحهم التى طرحوها فى النهر مقترعين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r4.claim: The clause depends on an omitted phrase: they cast the pens to see who would care for her, to learn the result, or as a spoken question.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r4.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف دل عليه يلقون كأنه قيل يلقونها ينظرون أيهم يكفل مريم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r5.claim: Their dispute was a competition over who would be Mary’s guardian.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p154/r5.anchor: فى شأنها تنافسا فى التكفل بها

BURSEVI:v2p27/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p27/r1.claim: That refers to the stories of Hannah, Mary, Jesus, Zachariah, and John.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r1.anchor: ما ذكرنا في القصص من حديث حنة ومريم وعيسى وزكريا ويحيى

BURSEVI:v2p27/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p27/r2.claim: Unseen news is available only by witnessing it, reading a book, learning from a scholar, or revelation; the first three means were absent for Muhammad, so revelation is the explanation.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r2.anchor: التي لا يوقف عليها إلا بمشاهدة أو قراءة كتاب أو تعلم من عالم أو بوحي من عند الله

BURSEVI:v2p27/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p27/r3.claim: The revelation of these stories proves Muhammad's prophethood and establishes an argument against those disputing him.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r3.anchor: دلالة على صحة نبوتك وإلزاما على من يحاجونك من الكفار

BURSEVI:v2p27/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p27/r4.claim: Quranic waḥy can mean revelation to prophets, inspiration, conveying a desired meaning, or a signal; all senses share the idea of informing in concealment.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r4.anchor: والوحي في القرآن لمعان للإرسال إلى الأنبياء

BURSEVI:v2p27/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p27/r5.claim: Muhammad's absence from the disputants over Mary's care confirms revelation; deniers know he neither read books nor learned these stories from scholars, and eyewitnessing was impossible.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r5.anchor: عند الذين اختلفوا وتنازعوا في تربية مريم وهو تقرير لكونه وحيا

BURSEVI:v2p27/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r6.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v2p27/r6.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh says deniers have only the absurd alternative of claiming eyewitnessing; they abandon the proven explanation of miracles for an impossible one, exposing their foolishness.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r6.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ في حواشيه : كأنه قيل : أيها المنكرون لأن أوحي إليه والمتهمون في دعوى نبوته

BURSEVI:v2p27/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p27/r7.claim: The priests cast their pens used to write the Torah as a blessed way to draw lots over who would care for Mary.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r7.anchor: التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة اختاروها للقرعة تبركا بها

BURSEVI:v2p27/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p27/r8.claim: The phrase is linked to an omitted verb indicated by cast: they cast the pens to see or learn which person would care for Mary.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r8.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف دل عليه يلقون أقلامهم أي : يلقونها ينظرون أو ليعلموا

BURSEVI:v2p27/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v2p27/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v2p27/r9.claim: The final clause refers to their dispute over Mary's care, already recounted above.
BURSEVI:v2p27/r9.anchor: في شأنها تنافسا في كفالتها وقد ذكر فيما سبق

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r1.claim: That refers to accounts of Zakariya, Yaḥyā, and Mary as reports from the unseen.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r1.anchor: أي الذي ذكرنا من حديث زكريا ويحيى ومريم عليهم السلام من أخبار الغيب

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r2.claim: These stories reached Muhammad without his reading scripture and were confirmed by the People of the Book, evidencing his prophethood.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r2.anchor: فيه دلالة على نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حيث أخبر عن قصة زكريا ومريم ولم يكن قرأ الكتب

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r3.claim: Wahy here means sending revelation; more broadly it means secret communication, including inspiration, gesture, and command.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r3.anchor: والإيحاء هنا الإرسال إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم. والوحي يكون إلهاما وإيماء وغير ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r4.speaker: العجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r4.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj uses awḥā for commanding the earth to settle.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r4.anchor: قال العجاج: أوحى لها القرار فاستقرت أي أمر الأرض بالقرار

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r5.claim: The hadith phrase الوحي الوحي means speed; its verb is tawahaytu.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث: «الوحي الوحي» وهو السرعة والفعل منه توحيت توحيا

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r6.speaker: ابن فارس
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r6.claim: Ibn Fāris defines wahy as gesture, writing, message, or secret communication; further examples include speed, sound, and calling for help.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r6.anchor: قال ابن فارس: الوحي الإشارة والكتابة والرسالة، وكل ما ألقيته إلى غيرك حتى يعلمه وحي كيف كان

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r7.claim: The address means Muhammad was not present with them.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r7.anchor: أي وما كنت يا محمد لديهم، أي بحضرتهم وعندهم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r8.claim: Aqlām is the plural of qalam, from the verb meaning to cut it.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r8.anchor: جمع قلم من قلمه إذا قطعه

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r9.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r9.claim: One view takes the pens as divining arrows or lots.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r10.claim: He prefers pens used to write the Torah because azlām are forbidden, though their casting might differ from pagan lots.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r10.anchor: وقيل: أقلامهم التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة، وهو أجود لأن الأزلام قد نهى الله عنها

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r11.claim: They disputed who would take Mary into custody; Zakariya claimed her because her aunt was with him, while Israelites claimed the scholar’s daughter.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r11.anchor: أي يحضنها، فقال زكريا: أنا أحق بها، خالتها عندي

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r12.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r12.claim: They put their pens in flowing water; whoever’s pen stayed still would have custody.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44/r12.anchor: وجاء كل واحد بقلمه، واتفقوا أن يجعلوا الأقلام في الماء الجاري فمن وقف قلمه

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r1.claim: The Prophet’s report says the pens flowed and Zakariya’s pen rose above the others, a sign for a prophet.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r2.claim: The interrogative clause is a subject and predicate in an accusative slot supplied by an implied verb; ayy is not governed because interrogative.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r2.anchor: ابتداء وخبر في موضع نصب بالفعل المضمر الذي دل عليه الكلام التقدير: ينظرون أيهم يكفل مريم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r3.speaker: بعض علمائنا
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r3.claim: Some scholars infer lots are valid for fair division among equals, reassuring them and removing suspicion of favoritism.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r3.anchor: استدل بعض علمائنا بهذه الآية على إثبات القرعة، وهي أصل في شرعنا لكل من أراد العدل في القسمة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r4.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r4.claim: Most jurists call lots sunna for equal claimants, avoiding favoritism when shares are alike.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r4.anchor: وهي سنة عند جمهور الفقهاء في المستويين في الحجة ليعدل بينهم وتطمئن قلوبهم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa and his followers reject lots and their reports as meaningless and like forbidden divining arrows.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r5.anchor: ورد العمل بالقرعة أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، وردوا الأحاديث الواردة فيها، وزعموا أنها لا معنى لها

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir also reports Abū Ḥanīfa allowing lots despite their failure by analogy, relying on reports and sunna.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r6.anchor: وحكى ابن المنذر عن أبي حنيفة أنه جوزها وقال: القرعة في القياس لا تستقيم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says Jonah, Zakariya, and Muhammad were three prophets who used lots.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: وقد عمل بالقرعة ثلاثة من الأنبياء: يونس وزكريا ونبينا محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r8.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r8.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says lots to divide among partners is effectively consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن المنذر. واستعمال القرعة كالإجماع من أهل العلم فيما يقسم بين الشركاء

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r9.speaker: النعمان بن بشير
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r9.claim: Al-Bukhārī cites the Prophet’s ship parable about upholding or neglecting God’s limits and drawing lots for places.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r10.speaker: أم العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r10.claim: The Anṣār drew lots for migrant lodging; ʿUthmān ibn Maẓʿūn drew his share.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r10.anchor: وحديث أم العلاء، وأن عثمان بن مظعون طار لهم سهمه في السكنى حين اقترعت الأنصار سكنى المهاجرين

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r11.speaker: عائشة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r11.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports the Prophet drew lots among his wives before travel and took the one whose lot came out.

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r12.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r12.claim: Mālik is reported both to draw lots for travel and to choose the wife most suited to the journey.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r12.anchor: وقد اختلفت الرواية عن مالك في ذلك فقال مرة: يقرع للحديث. وقال مرة: يسافر بأوفقهن له في السفر

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r13.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r13.claim: The Prophet says people would draw lots for the call to prayer and first row if they knew their reward.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#2/r13.anchor: وحديث أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r1.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa argues lots were unnecessary because Mary’s guardianship and the Prophet’s travel choices could be settled by consent.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r1.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة بأن قال: إن القرعة في شأن زكريا وأزواج النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r2.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says that is weak: lots reveal a decision when people contest a coveted matter, unlike agreement.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r2.anchor: قال ابن العربي: «وهذا ضعيف، لأن القرعة إنما فائدتها استخراج الحكم الخفي عند التشاح

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r3.speaker: الشافعي ومن قال بها
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī’s method uses equal slips with claimants’ names in clay pellets, dried, hidden by an absent person, then drawn to assign shares.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r3.anchor: وصفة القرعة عند الشافعي ومن قال بها: أن تقطع رقاع صغار مستوية فيكتب في كل رقعة اسم ذي السهم

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r4.claim: The maternal aunt has custody priority over other relatives except the grandmother.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r4.anchor: ودلت الآية أيضا على أن الخالة أحق بالحضانة من سائر القرابات ما عدا الجدة

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r5.claim: The Prophet assigned Hamza’s daughter Ummat Allah to Jaʿfar because her aunt was with him, saying an aunt is like a mother.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r5.anchor: وقد قضى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في ابنة حمزة واسمها أمة الله لجعفر وكانت عنده خالتها

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r6.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r6.claim: Abū Dāwūd says ʿAlī, Jaʿfar, and Zayd claimed Hamza’s daughter; the Prophet assigned her to Jaʿfar and her aunt.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r6.anchor: وخرج أبو داود عن علي قال

QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r7.speaker: ابن أبي خيثمة
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r7.claim: Ibn Abī Khaythama says Zayd was Hamza’s executor, so the aunt outranks an executor; a cousin who is her husband does not displace her, even if not her maḥram.
QURTUBI-FULL:3:44#3/r7.anchor: وذكر ابن أبي خيثمة أن زيد بن حارثة كان وصي حمزة، فتكون الخالة على هذا أحق من الوصي

RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r1.claim: That points to the preceding account of Hannah, Zechariah, John, and Jesus, unseen information known to the Prophet only through revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم ، والمعنى أن الذي مضى ذكره من حديث حنة وزكريا ويحيى وعيسى بن مريم

RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r2.claim: The opponents knew Muhammad had not learned by reading or hearing yet denied revelation, so the verse sarcastically denies his having witnessed events they knew he could not have witnessed.
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r2.anchor: فلم يبق إلا المشاهدة ، وهي وإن كانت في غاية الاستبعاد إلا أنها نفيت على سبيل التهكم بالمنكرين للوحي

RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r3.claim: Anbāʾ are reports about what is absent from one's knowledge; waḥy covers covert communication by signs, writing, or other means, including inspiration.
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r3.anchor: الأنباء : الإخبار عما غاب عنك ، وأما الإيحاء فقد ورد الكتاب به على معان مختلفة

RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r4.claim: God conveyed these events to the Prophet through Gabriel in a manner hidden from others, so the communication is called revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r4.anchor: فلما كان الله سبحانه ألقى هذه الأشياء إلى الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بواسطة جبريل عليه السلام بحيث يخفى ذلك على غيره

RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r5.claim: Most commentators identify the lots as their pens for writing the Torah and other scriptures; the one whose pen moved against the current won, and Zechariah's did.
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r5.anchor: المراد بالأقلام التي كانوا يكتبون بها التوراة وسائر كتب الله تعالى ، وكان القراع على أن كل من جرى قلمه

RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r6.speaker: الربيع
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r6.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says they cast their staffs into running water, and Zechariah's staff moved against the current and prevailed.
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r6.anchor: هذا قول الربيع والثالث : قال أبو مسلم : معنى يلقون أقلامهم مما كانت الأمم تفعله

RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r7.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r7.claim: Abū Muslim reads the phrase as drawing lots by casting marked slips bearing their names; the winner took responsibility for Mary, like drawing arrows for shares of a camel.
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r7.anchor: قال أبو مسلم : معنى يلقون أقلامهم مما كانت الأمم تفعله من المساهمة عند التنازع فيطرحون منها ما يكتبون عليها أسماءهم

RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r8.claim: Abū Muslim explains that the lots can be called pens because they are cut and sharpened; anything trimmed piece by piece is said to be qalam-ed.
RAZI-FULL:v8p40/r8.anchor: وإنما سميت هذه السهام أقلاما لأنها تقلم وتبرى ، وكل ما قطعت منه شيئا بعد شيء فقد قلمته

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r1.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r1.claim: Al-Qāḍī says derivation permits calling rods or lots pens, but common usage restricts qalam to writing instruments, which must therefore be intended.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r1.anchor: قال القاضي : وقوع لفظ القلم على هذه الأشياء وإن كان صحيحا نظرا إلى أصل الاشتقاق ، إلا أن العرف أوجب اختصاص القلم بهذا الذي يكتب به

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r2.claim: The verse establishes a lot distinguishing the candidate deserving custody but does not specify how it was cast; a report says the pens were cast in water and whoever moved against its current won, which happened for Zechariah.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r2.anchor: إلا أنه روي في الخبر أنهم كانوا يلقونها في الماء بشرط أن من جرى قلمه على خلاف جري الماء فاليد له

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r3.speaker: قال بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r3.claim: One explanation for their eagerness to care for Mary is that her father, ʿImrān, had been their leader and chief.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r3.anchor: فقال بعضهم : إن عمران أباها كان رئيسا لهم ومقدما عليهم ، فلأجل حق أبيها رغبوا في كفالتها

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r4.speaker: قال بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r4.claim: Another explanation is that Mary's mother had dedicated her to God's worship and service in the sanctuary, prompting their eagerness to take her in.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن أمها حررتها لعبادة الله تعالى ولخدمة بيت الله تعالى ، ولأجل ذلك حرصوا

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r5.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r5.claim: Others say the scriptures disclosed Mary's and Jesus's future significance, which made them compete to care for her.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل لأن في الكتب الإلاهية كان بيان أمرها وأمر عيسى عليه السلام حاصلا

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r6.speaker: منهم من قال
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r6.claim: One view identifies the disputants as the sanctuary's attendants.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r6.anchor: فمنهم من قال : كانوا هم خدمة البيت ، ومنهم من قال : بل العلماء والأحبار وكتاب الوحي

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r7.speaker: منهم من قال
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r7.claim: Another view identifies them as scholars, religious authorities, and scribes of revelation; al-Rāzī adds that they were leading people of religious merit and devotion.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r7.anchor: ومنهم من قال : بل العلماء والأحبار وكتاب الوحي ، ولا شبهة في أنهم كانوا من الخواص وأهل الفضل في الدين

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r8.claim: The clause omits an understood purpose: they cast their pens in order to see which of them would care for Mary.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r8.anchor: ففيه حذف والتقدير : يلقون أقلامهم لينظروا أيهم يكفل مريم وإنما حسن لكونه معلوما

RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r9.claim: The dispute concerns their drawing lots and arguing over Mary's custody; it may have occurred before or after the lot, and the point is their intense desire to care for her, prompted by her mother's prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v8p41/r9.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون المراد بهذا الاختصام ما كان قبل الإقراع ، ويحتمل أن يكون اختصاما آخر حصل بعد الإقراع
